metadata.title: Boston Public Schools — Parent Summary Guide
metadata.description: ~500-word parent-facing summaries for all 134 BPS school sites, synthesizing official BPS profiles, NCES data, Wikipedia, and school websites. Each entry covers school identity, programs, admissions process, and key considerations for enrolling families.
metadata.important_notice: Several BPS schools are subject to active closure, merger, or reconfiguration proceedings as of March 2026. Schools flagged with 'IMPORTANT' in their operational_notes field must be verified directly with BPS before any enrollment decision. Status: bostonpublicschools.org or call a BPS Welcome Center.

schools.name: Guild Elementary
schools.summary: Curtis Guild Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in East Boston's Orient Heights area. With approximately 247 students, it is one of the smaller elementary schools in the East Boston cluster, lending it an intimate community feel. The school has earned recognition as a DESE School of Recognition in prior years, signaling above-average academic growth and achievement on MCAS. Guild's culture centers on high expectations for every student regardless of background. The school draws a highly diverse student body reflecting East Boston's large immigrant population, primarily families of Latin American origin. Pre-K programming is offered at K0 and K1 levels, making it a viable early entry point. Families should know that elementary assignment in East Boston follows BPS's home-based plan — proximity boosts chances but does not guarantee placement. All Boston families may apply, though East Boston residents receive geographic priority. Because East Boston is separated from the rest of the city by the harbor, families living here are guaranteed a seat somewhere in East Boston at K2 and above, providing added peace of mind. Class sizes typically run 20–25 students. Enrichment and after-school programming vary year to year; families should inquire directly. Guild is a solid neighborhood choice for families who prioritize a community-rooted school with a commitment to equity and academic excellence.

schools.name: Kennedy Patrick Elem
schools.operational_notes: Named 2024–2025 DESE School of Recognition.
schools.summary: Patrick J. Kennedy Elementary School is the standout academic performer in the East Boston elementary cluster, earning the prestigious 2024–2025 DESE School of Recognition designation — one of the most meaningful academic honors a Massachusetts public school can receive. With approximately 267 students in grades PK–6, the school delivers consistently strong MCAS achievement and growth despite serving a predominantly English Learner, immigrant-background community — a context that makes the recognition especially impressive, as it demonstrates the school is serving all students well. The school culture emphasizes high expectations, consistent instructional practices, and family partnership. Pre-K seats (K0/K1) are available but limited and not guaranteed; K2 is guaranteed for all East Boston applicants. East Boston families receive home-based geographic priority, and the neighborhood seat guarantee ensures K2 placement somewhere in East Boston. Families who prioritize documented academic outcomes will find Kennedy Patrick to be among the most compelling neighborhood elementary options in East Boston. Inquire about after-school programs, enrichment activities, and English Learner service models when visiting.

schools.name: Otis Elementary
schools.summary: Otis Elementary is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in East Boston's Jeffries Point area, generally regarded as one of the better-performing elementary schools in the local cluster. The school draws a diverse, predominantly Latino and immigrant-background student body and maintains a welcoming, community-focused environment emphasizing family engagement and culturally responsive teaching. Like all East Boston elementary schools, Otis benefits from the geographic seat guarantee ensuring East Boston families are placed somewhere in the neighborhood for K2 and above. Pre-K seats (K0/K1) are available but not guaranteed. Assignment follows BPS's home-based plan. Families should attend BPS School Information Sessions in the fall to learn more. As a neighborhood school serving many English Learners, Otis invests in multilingual supports. Specific enrichment offerings and after-school programming should be confirmed directly with the school. Otis Elementary is a dependable, community-connected neighborhood option for East Boston families in the Jeffries Point area.

schools.name: O'Donnell Elementary
schools.summary: O'Donnell Elementary is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in East Boston with approximately 275 students. The school serves a diverse, largely Latino and immigrant student population and provides English Learner services for students still developing English proficiency. Full-day K2 is provided (age-5 cutoff September 1), and limited K0/K1 pre-K seats are available but not guaranteed. Assignment follows BPS's home-based plan with East Boston residents receiving priority. East Boston families benefit from the neighborhood seat guarantee — if O'Donnell is unavailable, another East Boston school will be assigned for K2 and above. The school creates a safe, welcoming environment for students of diverse backgrounds. Families should visit, attend information sessions, and ask about academic programs, extracurricular offerings, and English Learner supports. O'Donnell is a solid community-centered neighborhood elementary option for East Boston families in the central neighborhood.

schools.name: East Boston High
schools.admissions: Citywide — all Boston residents may apply. No exam required.
schools.summary: East Boston High School is a comprehensive neighborhood high school serving grades 9–12 with approximately 1,200 students, and one of the larger BPS high schools. While technically citywide and open to all Boston residents, it draws primarily from East Boston's neighborhoods and reflects the area's deep immigrant heritage — students from dozens of countries of origin, many of whom are English Learners or Recent Arrivals. Multilingual and multicultural competency is a defining feature of school life. The school offers Career and Technical Education pathways allowing students to earn industry credentials alongside their academic diplomas. All BPS high schools are citywide, so any Boston resident may apply. Students from East Boston elementary and K–8 schools often stay for high school here, providing continuity. Families should ask about specific CTE pathway options, graduation rates, college acceptance data, AP and dual enrollment opportunities, and extracurricular sports and clubs. The school is accessible by MBTA Blue Line. East Boston High is the right choice for families who want a larger comprehensive high school with a strong community identity, vocational pathways, and a welcoming environment for English Learners.

schools.name: Umana/Alighieri K-8
special_programs: Special Olympics National Banner Unified Champion School 2024–2025
schools.operational_notes: Named Special Olympics National Banner Unified Champion School 2024–2025.
schools.summary: Mario Umana Academy (Umana/Alighieri K-8) is one of the largest K–8 schools in BPS at approximately 632 students and earned national distinction in 2024–2025 as a Special Olympics National Banner Unified Champion School — recognizing outstanding work integrating students with and without disabilities into shared sports and activities. This makes Umana an exceptional choice for families of children with disabilities who want a school where inclusion is genuinely embedded in culture, not just policy. The school also offers a Piano Lab, providing music education relatively uncommon at the K–8 level in BPS. With over 600 students, Umana has the scale to support broad programming and extracurriculars that smaller schools cannot. The student body is highly diverse, primarily Latino and immigrant families reflecting East Boston demographics. The K–8 configuration means families stay in one building through middle school, avoiding a separate middle school application. East Boston families receive geographic priority under home-based assignment. Families should ask about after-school programs, sports, eighth-grade transition support, and special education services. Umana is particularly recommended for families with children who have IEPs or who value inclusive community athletics.

schools.name: East Boston EEC
schools.admissions: Apply through BPS enrollment. K0/K1 seats NOT guaranteed. Most K0 seats reserved for students with disabilities.
schools.operational_notes: Serves ages 3–4 only. Children transition to K2 at an elementary school after K1.
schools.summary: East Boston Early Education Center is a dedicated BPS early childhood center serving children ages 3–4 through K0 and K1 pre-K programs. One of a small number of standalone early education centers in BPS, it provides a developmentally appropriate, nurturing environment before children transition to full-day K2 at an elementary school. The school emphasizes strong partnership among teachers, staff, and families. Parents must understand that K0 (age 3) placements are extremely limited — most K0 seats are reserved for students with disabilities identified through BPS's Child Find process. K1 (age 4) seats have broader availability but are still not guaranteed. Priority registration runs January through early February each year; children must be 3 (K0) or 4 (K1) by September 1. After K1, families apply separately for K2 at an elementary school — K2 placement is guaranteed for all BPS applicants, though not at a specific school. East Boston EEC is a strong option for families who want to start their child's public school experience in a small, community-focused early childhood setting. Families should also explore the Great Starts platform at bostonpublicschools.org for the full picture of BPS and community childcare options in East Boston.

schools.name: McKay K-8
schools.summary: Donald McKay K–8 School is one of the largest K–8 schools in the BPS portfolio with approximately 670 students from pre-K through grade 8 in East Boston. Its size enables a broader range of programming, extracurriculars, and staffing than smaller schools can support. The K–8 configuration means families can avoid the middle school application process entirely, remaining in one building from kindergarten through eighth grade. McKay serves a predominantly Latino, immigrant-origin student body and provides robust English Learner services for students developing English proficiency. Older students serve as role models for younger ones in the multi-age community. Families should ask about middle school elective offerings, sports and extracurriculars, and eighth-grade high school transition counseling. East Boston families receive home-based priority, and all East Boston families are guaranteed a K2 placement somewhere in the neighborhood. McKay is a strong community-connected K–8 choice for East Boston families who value school continuity and a large, well-resourced neighborhood school.

schools.name: Adams Elementary
schools.summary: Adams Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in East Boston, located on Webster Street. The school serves a diverse community with a significant proportion of Latino and immigrant-background students and provides English Learner services central to East Boston's school landscape. Full-day K2 is provided for age-5 students, and pre-K seats at K0/K1 are available but limited and not guaranteed. Assignment follows BPS's home-based plan with East Boston geographic priority. The East Boston neighborhood seat guarantee means K2 placement is assured somewhere in the neighborhood even if Adams is not assigned. The school emphasizes family engagement and a supportive learning environment. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, extracurriculars, and English Learner supports. Adams is a solid community-anchored elementary choice for families in East Boston's Webster Street corridor.

schools.name: Bradley Elementary
schools.operational_notes: Among highest-performing elementary schools in East Boston cluster.
schools.summary: Bradley Elementary School is consistently regarded as one of the top-performing elementary schools in the East Boston cluster. MCAS data indicates that approximately 60% of Bradley students score at or above proficiency in English Language Arts — significantly exceeding the BPS district average and placing Bradley among the strongest-performing neighborhood elementary schools in the city. The school serves pre-kindergarten through grade 6 with approximately 280 students, giving it a manageable size that supports personalized teacher-student-family relationships. Its strong academic outcomes in a predominantly immigrant community reflect a culture of high expectations and consistent instruction. Home-based assignment gives East Boston families geographic priority; K2 is guaranteed for all East Boston applicants, though not necessarily at Bradley. Families who prioritize MCAS performance will find Bradley among the most compelling neighborhood elementary options in East Boston. Inquire about after-school programs and English Learner supports when visiting.

schools.name: Alighieri Montessori
schools.school_type: Traditional district school with Montessori program
schools.summary: Alighieri Montessori School is one of the few BPS schools offering a Montessori-model curriculum, making it a distinctive option for East Boston families. The school serves pre-kindergarten through grade 6 and applies Montessori principles across classrooms: child-directed learning in structured environments, mixed-age groupings, hands-on materials, and emphasis on intrinsic motivation and independence rather than rote instruction. Montessori education has a strong evidence base for developing self-regulation, problem-solving, and early literacy and math skills. For families who value Montessori pedagogy or whose children thrive in exploratory, less rigid environments, Alighieri offers a genuinely differentiated public school model at no cost. The school is on Gove Street in East Boston near the East Boston Early Education Center. Assignment follows home-based plan with East Boston priority. Families should ask how Montessori principles are implemented in grades 4–6, how the school supports the middle school transition, and what progress monitoring looks like within the Montessori framework. For East Boston families seeking an alternative to traditional classroom instruction within the public system, Alighieri Montessori is a rare and valuable option.

schools.name: Harvard/Kent Elem
schools.admissions: Home-based assignment; Chinese SEI families may access citywide. Contact BPS Multilingual Office.
schools.operational_notes: One of only three BPS schools with Chinese SEI.
schools.summary: Harvard/Kent Elementary in Charlestown hosts one of only three Chinese Sheltered English Immersion (SEI) language-specific programs in all of BPS, making it a citywide destination for Chinese-speaking families who want their elementary-aged children to receive academic support in their home language while developing English proficiency. Chinese SEI research consistently shows that native-language academic support accelerates long-term English acquisition and academic achievement — making Harvard/Kent's program particularly valuable for families from Boston's large Chinese-speaking community. The broader school serves PK–6 with approximately 340 students, reflecting Charlestown's increasingly diverse demographics. For non-Chinese-speaking families, Harvard/Kent is a solid neighborhood elementary with the full BPS curriculum. Home-based assignment applies for local families; Chinese SEI families may be eligible for citywide access. Families interested in the SEI track should contact BPS's Office of Multilingual and Multicultural Education for eligibility and application details. Harvard/Kent is an excellent Charlestown neighborhood school and an especially valuable resource for Boston's Chinese-speaking community at the elementary level.

schools.name: Charlestown High
schools.admissions: Citywide — all Boston residents may apply. No exam required.
schools.operational_notes: Absorbed Edwards Middle School grades after 2021 closure.
schools.summary: Charlestown High School is a comprehensive citywide high school serving grades 9–12 with approximately 700 students, and one of only three BPS schools hosting a Chinese Sheltered English Immersion (SEI) program — making it a key resource for Chinese-speaking English Learners at the high school level. For Chinese-speaking families with high school-aged students needing language support, Charlestown High is one of the very few options in BPS that provides Chinese-language SEI at the secondary level. After the closure of the Clarence R. Edwards Middle School in 2021, Charlestown High absorbed those middle school grades, strengthening its community anchor role. The school draws from Charlestown and citywide, serving a diverse mix of backgrounds and language needs. All BPS high schools are citywide, so any Boston resident may apply. Families should ask about AP course offerings, graduation and college acceptance rates, sports and extracurriculars, and specific English Learner supports. Charlestown High is appropriate for families seeking a larger comprehensive high school with strong multilingual programming in a neighborhood with rich community history.

schools.name: Edwards Middle
schools.operational_notes: IMPORTANT: The original Clarence R. Edwards Middle School was closed in 2021, with grades merged into Charlestown High. Verify current operating status directly with BPS before applying.
schools.summary: Edwards Middle School is listed in BPS records at 28 Walker Street in Charlestown for the 2024–2025 school year. Families must be aware of a critical operational note: the original Clarence R. Edwards Middle School was voted for closure by the Boston School Committee in 2021, with seventh and eighth grade programs absorbed into Charlestown High School. The presence of this address in current BPS records may indicate a reconstituted or renamed program at this location, or an administrative listing. Before making any enrollment decisions based on Edwards Middle, families must contact BPS's Office of Enrollment directly to confirm whether the school is actively enrolling students, what grades it serves, and its current operational status. Charlestown families seeking confirmed middle school options should use BPS's home-based assignment tool and speak with an enrollment specialist. Always verify school status at bostonpublicschools.org before submitting any application.

schools.name: Warren/Prescott
special_programs: Special Olympics National Banner Unified Champion School 2024–2025
schools.operational_notes: Named Special Olympics National Banner Unified Champion School 2024–2025.
schools.summary: Warren-Prescott K–8 School is Charlestown's primary K–8 school and was honored as a Special Olympics National Banner Unified Champion School for 2024–2025 — one of a small number of BPS schools to earn this prestigious national recognition. The designation reflects the school's outstanding commitment to inclusive sports and activities that genuinely integrate students with and without disabilities into shared teams and community events, going well beyond compliance to create a true inclusion culture. For families of children with disabilities or those who value inclusive school environments, this recognition is a powerful indicator of school culture and community. Warren-Prescott serves kindergarten through grade 8, allowing families to remain in one school through middle school without a separate application. The school sits in Charlestown's historic core and draws from the neighborhood's diverse and mixed-income community. Families should inquire about academic programs, enrichment, middle school electives, Special Olympics Unified Sports programs, and eighth-grade high school transition planning. Assignment follows BPS's home-based plan with Charlestown residents receiving priority. Warren-Prescott is a strong all-around K–8 option — and particularly compelling for families with children who have disabilities or who prioritize genuine inclusive school culture.

schools.name: Eliot K-8
schools.admissions: Home-based assignment. Note: also listed at 585 Commercial Street in some BPS records — verify current campus with BPS.
schools.summary: Eliot K–8 School is located in Boston's historic North End neighborhood and serves kindergarten through grade 8. The school is a community anchor for one of Boston's most densely populated and historically significant neighborhoods — the North End has a mix of long-established families and newer residents, and Eliot serves as its primary neighborhood school. As a K–8, Eliot allows students to complete elementary and middle school years in a single building, avoiding the transition disruption of a separate middle school application. The school benefits from the North End's engaged parent community. Families should note that BPS records show two addresses for Eliot K–8 (16 Charter Street and 585 Commercial Street) — this may reflect a building transition or administrative distinction, so families should confirm the current primary campus when contacting the school. Assignment follows BPS's home-based plan, with North End and Downtown families receiving priority. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school offerings, middle school elective options, and sports and clubs. Eliot K–8 is a strong neighborhood school for families in the North End who value K–8 continuity and a community-rooted identity.

schools.name: Quincy Upper School
special_programs: International Baccalaureate (IB) Middle Years and Diploma Programme
K–12 pathway with Quincy Lower Elementary
schools.admissions: Pilot school with lottery. Apply during BPS priority registration (January–February) for grade 6.
schools.operational_notes: IB-accredited. Part of K–12 IB pathway with Josiah Quincy Lower School.
schools.summary: Josiah Quincy Upper School is one of the most academically distinguished schools in BPS — a pilot school with International Baccalaureate (IB) accreditation at both the middle and high school levels, serving grades 6–12. As a pilot school, Quincy Upper has autonomy over budget, staffing, curriculum, and calendar, freedoms that enable it to sustain the rigorous IB framework. The IB is a globally recognized college-preparatory credential emphasizing critical thinking, international-mindedness, and research skills, and the IB Diploma Programme (grades 11–12) is recognized by universities worldwide as among the strongest academic credentials available. Quincy Upper also offers a one-way Chinese bilingual program for families whose home language is Chinese — the only secondary school in BPS combining IB programming with Chinese-language instruction. The school forms a rare K–12 pathway with Josiah Quincy Lower (Elementary), meaning students can follow an IB curriculum from kindergarten through grade 12 without interruption. Located in Downtown Boston near Chinatown and accessible by MBTA, the school draws students citywide. Families should apply during the January–February priority registration window and attend the school's information session. Quincy Upper School is one of the strongest options in BPS for academically motivated students, particularly Chinese-speaking families seeking IB programming and bilingual support.

schools.name: Quincy Lower (K-5)
schools.admissions: Home-based assignment; IB and bilingual programming available to all enrolled students.
schools.operational_notes: IB PYP accredited. Pathway to Quincy Upper School (grades 6–12).
schools.summary: Josiah Quincy Lower School is a BPS elementary school serving grades K–5 in Downtown Boston and Chinatown, and one of the few BPS elementary schools with International Baccalaureate Primary Years Programme (PYP) accreditation. The IB PYP is a research-backed inquiry-based learning framework emphasizing international-mindedness and whole-child development from the earliest grades. The school also offers a one-way Chinese bilingual program for students whose home language is Chinese, providing Chinese-language academic support while building English proficiency — a model shown to be highly effective for long-term bilingualism and academic success. Quincy Lower is the entry point of a K–12 IB pathway: students completing K–5 here can continue to Josiah Quincy Upper School (grades 6–12), maintaining the IB framework and Chinese bilingual programming through high school. Located near Chinatown and South Station, it is highly accessible by MBTA from across Boston. Chinatown and Downtown families receive home-based priority; others may apply through standard BPS enrollment. Quincy Lower is one of the most distinctive and academically ambitious elementary options in BPS — an outstanding choice for Chinese-speaking families and any family seeking rigorous IB programming from kindergarten onward.

schools.name: Snowden International
schools.admissions: Citywide — all Boston residents may apply. No exam required.
schools.summary: Muriel S. Snowden International School at Copley is a grades 6–12 citywide school on Newbury Street in Boston's Back Bay, one of the most accessible and prominently located schools in the BPS system. The school's defining feature is its international curriculum focus — emphasizing global perspectives, world language instruction, and the cross-cultural competency valued in higher education and the workplace. Citywide status means any Boston resident may apply regardless of home neighborhood. Located steps from the Copley Square MBTA stop, the school is reachable from any neighborhood. The school serves a diverse student population and a 6–12 structure allows for a long, continuous relationship between students and the school community. Families should ask about which world languages are offered, AP and dual enrollment opportunities, college counseling, graduation and college acceptance rates, and extracurricular programs. Priority registration for grade 6 runs January through early February. Snowden is a good fit for families who value global education, language learning, and a school culture that celebrates international backgrounds.

schools.name: McKinley Elementary
schools.operational_notes: Co-located at McKinley/Mackey building with McKinley South End Academy.
schools.summary: McKinley Elementary School serves pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Boston's South End at the McKinley/Mackey building on Warren Avenue. The school offers a standard elementary curriculum in one of Boston's most diverse and culturally vibrant neighborhoods. The McKinley/Mackey building is a multi-school site also housing McKinley South End Academy (middle and high grades), so families will share the facility with older students. The South End's engaged parent community tends to translate into active family participation in school life. McKinley provides full-day K2 and limited K0/K1 pre-K seats, with assignment following BPS's home-based plan. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and how the multi-school building arrangement is managed day to day. For South End families looking for a neighborhood elementary school with a community feel, McKinley Elementary is a natural first option to explore.

schools.name: McKinley So. End Acad
schools.admissions: Home-based assignment for middle grades; citywide for high school.
schools.operational_notes: Verify current grade configuration with BPS — the school has undergone changes.
schools.summary: McKinley South End Academy serves grades 6–12 at the McKinley/Mackey building in the South End, co-located with McKinley Elementary. The school provides middle and high school programming for South End students and citywide applicants. Families should be aware that this school has undergone grade configuration changes in recent years; verifying the current grade span and enrollment details directly with BPS before applying is strongly recommended. As a high school, McKinley South End Academy is citywide and open to all Boston residents; middle school assignment is home-based. The South End location is well-served by MBTA. Families considering this school should ask about AP and elective course offerings, graduation and college outcomes, sports and extracurriculars, and student support services including counseling. For families already in the McKinley Elementary community, the same building offers a natural, familiar transition into middle and high school grades.

schools.name: McKinley Prep High Sch
schools.admissions: Citywide — all Boston residents may apply. No exam required.
schools.summary: McKinley Preparatory High School is a citywide BPS high school serving grades 9–12 in the Fenway area. Part of the McKinley Schools network, it operates on a smaller scale than comprehensive high schools like East Boston High or Brighton High — a potential advantage for students who benefit from a more intimate setting with closer teacher-student relationships. As a citywide school, McKinley Prep is open to all Boston residents regardless of home neighborhood. The Fenway location provides access to MBTA Green Line service, making commutes manageable from many parts of the city. Families should ask about course offerings, AP and dual enrollment options, graduation rates, college acceptance outcomes, extracurricular programs, and student support services. McKinley Prep is worth considering for families who want a citywide high school in the Fenway area, particularly those who prefer a smaller learning environment to the large comprehensive high schools in BPS.

schools.name: McKinley Middle
schools.summary: McKinley Middle School serves grades 6–8 in the Fenway area of Boston at 50 St. Mary Street, part of the McKinley Schools network. A dedicated middle school allows students to experience departmentalized instruction, expanded extracurriculars, and age-appropriate programming in a setting designed specifically for the middle school years. The Fenway location is accessible by MBTA Green Line. Families should ask about the core curriculum, available electives and enrichment, sports teams, after-school programs, and how the school supports the social-emotional needs of middle schoolers. Eighth-grade high school transition planning and counseling are also important questions to raise. Assignment follows BPS's home-based plan with priority for students in the Fenway, Mission Hill, and adjacent neighborhoods. McKinley Middle is a solid, accessible middle school option for families in these areas.

schools.name: Boston Arts Academy
special_programs: Professional arts training: visual art, music, theater, fashion design, dance
Dual academic and professional arts curriculum
schools.admissions: Citywide. Audition required in chosen art discipline. Apply during BPS priority registration; auditions begin November/December.
schools.operational_notes: Competitive audition-based admissions. Students choose one of five arts disciplines.
schools.summary: Boston Arts Academy (BAA) is one of the most distinctive and celebrated schools in BPS — a citywide pilot high school that genuinely integrates professional arts training with rigorous academics. BAA offers training in five disciplines: visual art, music, theater, fashion design, and dance. Admission is competitive and audition-based: students must audition in their chosen discipline during the enrollment period, with auditions beginning in November or December. The school serves approximately 440 students in grades 9–12, drawing from every Boston neighborhood. BAA's dual-curriculum model means students take standard academic courses alongside professional-level arts training from practicing artist-educators. Alumni go on to competitive colleges and conservatories, and many pursue careers in the arts and creative industries. As a pilot school, BAA has autonomy over its instructional model and staffing. Located in the Fenway near the Museum of Fine Arts and Northeastern University, the school benefits from partnerships with Boston's thriving arts ecosystem. Families should attend the school's information night, understand the audition timeline, and speak with current students. BAA is the right choice for passionate, artistically driven students who want a high school that treats artistic development as seriously as academic preparation.

schools.name: Boston Latin School
schools.admissions: Exam school. Admission to grades 7 and 9 only. Requires MAP Growth test and minimum B GPA. Highly competitive. Tiered by socioeconomic zone.
schools.operational_notes: Nation's oldest public school (founded 1635). Most selective school in BPS.
schools.summary: Boston Latin School (BLS) is the oldest public school in the United States (founded 1635) and the most academically selective school in BPS. As one of three exam schools, admission to grades 7 or 9 requires MAP Growth test scores and a minimum B average GPA. Boston is divided into eight socioeconomic tiers, and seats are allocated across tiers to ensure diversity while rewarding achievement. BLS enrolls approximately 2,400 students in grades 7–12 and offers a rigorous classical liberal arts curriculum including Latin (and sometimes ancient Greek), a full suite of AP courses, a community service graduation requirement, and a college-preparatory focus that has sent graduates to the nation's most competitive universities for centuries. The school is academically intense — the workload is demanding and students need strong study skills, intrinsic motivation, and family support to thrive. Families should have students take the MAP Growth test in grade 6 and maintain strong grades. The Fenway location is accessible by MBTA Green Line. BLS information sessions are held in the fall. Boston Latin School is the right choice for highly academically motivated students seeking the most rigorous public school curriculum in Boston.

schools.name: Kennedy Health Careers Academy
schools.address: 110 The Fenway / 10 Fenwood Road, Boston, MA 02115
schools.admissions: Citywide. Horace Mann Charter — apply during BPS enrollment. May involve additional application steps.
schools.operational_notes: Located near Longwood Medical Area. Listed at two addresses in BPS records.
schools.summary: Edward M. Kennedy Academy for Health Careers is a Horace Mann Charter School — a BPS-funded in-district charter — serving grades 9–12. Strategically located near the Longwood Medical Area, the school enables real partnerships with institutions like Boston Children's Hospital, Dana-Farber Cancer Institute, Brigham and Women's Hospital, and Harvard Medical School, giving students access to health career exposure, internships, and mentorship opportunities unmatched in the public school system. Health career pathways and early college programming allow students to earn college credits in high school, reducing the time and cost of college. For students interested in medicine, nursing, public health, biomedical research, or any allied health field, Kennedy Health Careers provides focused, experiential preparation far beyond a standard high school. As a Horace Mann Charter, the school is tuition-free and funded by BPS. All Boston residents may apply during the standard BPS enrollment window. The school is listed at two addresses (110 The Fenway and 10 Fenwood Road); families should confirm the primary address when visiting. Kennedy Health Careers Academy is one of the most distinctive and career-relevant high school choices in BPS for students with genuine interest in the health sciences.

schools.name: Boston Adult Tech Acad
special_programs: High school diploma pathway for ages 19–22
schools.admissions: Open to Boston residents ages 19–22. Not applicable for families enrolling minor children.
schools.operational_notes: Not applicable for standard K–12 family enrollment decisions.
schools.summary: Boston Adult Technical Academy is a BPS school specifically designed for young adults ages 19–22 who have not yet earned a high school diploma or credential. It is not a school for children under 18 and families will not encounter it during standard BPS enrollment for minor children. It is, however, an important resource for older youth and young adults who left high school before completion and are seeking a pathway back to education with a technical and vocational focus. The school provides a supportive adult-oriented learning environment acknowledging the different life circumstances of older students — many of whom may be working, parenting, or dealing with disruptions that interrupted earlier schooling. Technical and vocational programming prepares students for employment and further education alongside the academic coursework required for a diploma. Located in Downtown Boston with good MBTA access, it is reachable from across the city. Families with young adults ages 19–22 who are disconnected from traditional schooling should be aware of this school as a meaningful re-engagement option.

schools.name: Hurley Elementary
schools.operational_notes: Listed as 'Hurley Elementary' in some BPS documents but operates as a K–8.
schools.summary: Hurley K–8 School is a traditional BPS school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 8 in Boston's South End with approximately 349 students. Despite being listed as 'Hurley Elementary' in some BPS documents, the school fully operates as a K–8, meaning students who enroll in pre-K or kindergarten can remain through eighth grade without a separate middle school application — a significant benefit for families who want to reduce school transitions. The K–8 model builds long-term community bonds and the mentoring dynamic of older students guiding younger ones. The South End is one of Boston's most economically and culturally diverse neighborhoods, and Hurley reflects that richness. Home-based assignment gives South End families geographic priority. Families should ask about middle school programming in grades 6–8, available electives, sports, extracurriculars, the eighth-grade high school transition process, and after-school care. Hurley K–8 is a solid community school option for South End families who value K–8 continuity and a neighborhood-rooted identity.

schools.name: Blackstone Elementary
schools.summary: Blackstone Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Boston's South End on Shawmut Avenue. The school is a community anchor in one of Boston's most sought-after neighborhoods, drawing students from the surrounding South End blocks and the diverse families that call this area home. Blackstone benefits from the South End's engaged parent community, which typically translates into active family participation and supplemental resources. The school provides full-day K2 programming and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for South End residents. Families should ask about academic programs, enrichment offerings, after-school care, and English Learner services. For South End families looking for a neighborhood elementary school, Blackstone is a natural first-choice option — its Shawmut Avenue location makes it particularly convenient for families in that part of the neighborhood.

schools.name: Mason Elementary
schools.summary: Mason Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roxbury. Located on Norfolk Avenue, it serves one of Boston's historically significant Black communities and reflects Roxbury's diverse, predominantly African-American and Latino student population. Mason is a community school in the truest sense, drawing from the immediate neighborhood and maintaining close ties with local families and organizations. Like all BPS elementary schools, it provides full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, following BPS's home-based assignment plan with Roxbury geographic priority. The school serves a student population with high proportions of English Learners and students from lower-income households, making academic support services central to its mission. Families should ask about targeted reading and math interventions, after-school programming, and family engagement activities. Mason Elementary is a neighborhood option for Roxbury families who want a community-rooted school close to home.

schools.name: Orchard Gardens K-8
schools.admissions: Pilot school — home-based assignment with pilot lottery. Cape Verdean Creole SEI may have language-based priority.
schools.operational_notes: National model for arts-integrated school turnaround.
schools.summary: Orchard Gardens K–8 is one of BPS's most celebrated turnaround stories and a nationally cited model for arts-integrated education. A decade ago, the school replaced all sports and extracurricular activities with arts programming — drawing, music, drama, dance — and the results were dramatic: attendance rose, discipline issues fell, and academic achievement improved significantly. As a pilot school, it has autonomy over curriculum and staffing to maintain this distinctive model. The school also hosts a Cape Verdean Creole SEI program — one of only three in BPS — serving the significant Cape Verdean community in Roxbury and Dorchester. The K–8 configuration means students can stay from kindergarten through eighth grade. With approximately 520 students, Orchard Gardens has a diverse student body reflecting Roxbury's African-American, Latino, and Cape Verdean communities. Families should attend the school's information session and apply during the BPS priority registration window (January–February). For families who value the arts, arts-integrated learning, or who are from the Cape Verdean community, Orchard Gardens K–8 is one of the most compelling options in BPS.

schools.name: Timilty Middle
schools.operational_notes: IMPORTANT: Wikipedia notes the original Timilty was closed in 2022. This address appears in 2024–2025 BPS records. Verify current status directly with BPS before applying.
schools.summary: James P. Timilty Middle School is listed in BPS records at 205 Roxbury Street in Roxbury. Families must be aware of a critical note: external sources including Wikipedia indicate the original Timilty Middle School was voted for closure by the Boston School Committee in 2021 and closed at the end of the 2021–2022 school year. The presence of this address in current BPS records may indicate a reconstituted or renamed program at this location. Before making any enrollment decision based on Timilty Middle, families must contact BPS's Office of Enrollment to confirm whether the school is actively enrolling, what grades it serves, and its current status. Roxbury families seeking confirmed middle school options should use BPS's home-based assignment tool and speak with an enrollment specialist. Always verify school status at bostonpublicschools.org before submitting any application.

schools.name: Hale Elementary
schools.summary: Hale Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roxbury, located on Cedar Street. It serves one of Boston's historically significant neighborhoods and draws students primarily from the surrounding Roxbury community, reflecting the neighborhood's predominantly African-American and Latino student population. The school maintains a community-centered focus on academic achievement and family engagement. Hale provides full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, with assignment following BPS's home-based plan. The school benefits from district-wide supports for schools serving high proportions of English Learners and students from lower-income households. Families should ask about academic support programs, after-school care, extracurricular activities, and the school's family engagement approach. Hale Elementary is the neighborhood elementary option for Roxbury families in the Cedar Street corridor.

schools.name: Higginson/Lewis K-8
schools.summary: Higginson/Lewis K–8 School in Roxbury is notable for its unusually broad athletic programming: the school offers nine sports — a remarkable number for a K–8 and a real differentiator for families with children passionate about athletics. Sports programming supports physical development, teamwork, discipline, and school connectedness, all of which correlate with academic engagement and attendance. The K–8 configuration means students can stay in one building from kindergarten through eighth grade, building stable community relationships without a disruptive middle school transition. With approximately 430 students, the school draws from Roxbury's diverse African-American, Latino, and immigrant community. Home-based assignment gives Roxbury residents priority. Families should also ask about academic enrichment, after-school programs, and the eighth-grade high school transition support process. For Roxbury families — particularly those with children who love sports and want a community-connected K–8 experience — Higginson/Lewis K–8 is a strong and distinctive option.

schools.name: Haynes EEC
schools.admissions: Apply through BPS enrollment. K0/K1 seats NOT guaranteed. Most K0 seats reserved for students with disabilities.
schools.summary: Haynes Early Education Center on Blue Hill Avenue in Roxbury is a standalone BPS early childhood center providing K0 and K1 pre-K programming for children ages 3 and 4. Like all BPS early education centers, Haynes focuses exclusively on the pre-K years, offering a developmentally appropriate learning environment before children transition to full-day K2 at an elementary school. The center serves Roxbury families and reflects the neighborhood's predominantly African-American and Latino community. K0 (age 3) placements are extremely limited — most are reserved for students with identified disabilities — and K1 (age 4) placements are available but not guaranteed. Priority registration opens in January. Children completing K1 must apply separately for K2 at an elementary school; K2 placement is guaranteed for all BPS applicants, though not at a specific school. Families in Roxbury seeking early childhood education within the public system should also explore the Great Starts platform for the full picture of available options in the area.

schools.name: Ellis Elementary
schools.summary: Ellis Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roxbury, located on Walnut Avenue. It serves the Roxbury community with a standard elementary curriculum and commitment to family engagement. Like all Roxbury elementary schools, Ellis serves a predominantly African-American and Latino student population with high proportions of English Learners, and academic support services including multilingual instruction are central to its work. Home-based assignment gives Roxbury residents geographic priority, and K2 is guaranteed for all BPS applicants. Families should visit the school and ask about academic and enrichment programs, after-school care availability, and family engagement activities. Ellis Elementary is the neighborhood elementary option for Roxbury families in the Walnut Avenue corridor.

schools.name: Boston Latin Academy
schools.admissions: Exam school. Admission to grades 7 and 9. Requires MAP Growth test and minimum B GPA.
schools.operational_notes: Formerly Roxbury Memorial High School. One of three BPS exam schools.
schools.summary: Boston Latin Academy (BLA) is one of three BPS exam schools and one of the city's most academically distinguished public schools. Formerly Roxbury Memorial High School, BLA serves grades 7–12 with approximately 1,600 students. Like all exam schools, admission requires MAP Growth test scores and a minimum B GPA, with seats allocated across Boston's eight socioeconomic tiers to ensure diversity. BLA offers a rigorous college-preparatory curriculum with a full suite of AP courses, strong extracurriculars including athletics, arts, and academic clubs, and a dedicated college counseling program. Located near the Roxbury/Dorchester border, the school is accessible by MBTA Orange Line and multiple bus routes. Compared to Boston Latin School, BLA has a more diverse student body racially and economically, and the school prides itself on its inclusive, supportive community. For families with academically strong students who may not score at the level required for Boston Latin School, BLA is often the next-best exam school option — and represents an outstanding education in its own right. Families should have students take MAP Growth in grade 6 and maintain strong grades to be competitive.

schools.name: Hernandez K-8
schools.summary: Hernández K–8 School serves kindergarten through grade 8 in Roxbury, offering students and families continuity across elementary and middle school years within a single community. Named for Rafael Hernández, a beloved Puerto Rican composer and songwriter, the school has deep roots in Roxbury's Latino community and emphasizes culturally responsive teaching and family engagement. The K–8 configuration allows students to stay in one school from kindergarten through eighth grade, building long-term community bonds. Standard BPS curriculum is offered with home-based assignment priority for Roxbury residents. Families should ask about elective courses in middle school grades, extracurricular offerings, sports, and the school's eighth-grade high school transition support. Hernández K–8 is a community-centered option for Roxbury families who value cultural connection, K–8 continuity, and a supportive school environment.

schools.name: Mendell Elementary
schools.summary: Mendell Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roxbury, located on School Street adjacent to Hernández K–8. The school serves Roxbury's diverse community with a standard elementary curriculum and community-focused approach, providing full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats. Home-based assignment gives Roxbury residents priority. The school emphasizes family engagement and culturally inclusive education for its predominantly African-American and Latino student body. Families should ask about academic support programs, after-school care, and specific enrichment offerings. Mendell Elementary is the neighborhood elementary option for Roxbury families in the School Street area.

schools.name: Tobin K-8
schools.summary: Tobin K–8 School serves kindergarten through grade 8 in Roxbury on Smith Street near the Mission Hill neighborhood border, providing a K–8 pathway that allows students to remain in one school from kindergarten through middle school. The K–8 model reduces educational transitions and builds long-term community bonds among students and families. With approximately 360 students, Tobin serves Roxbury's diverse community and provides the full BPS elementary and middle curriculum. Home-based assignment gives Roxbury residents geographic priority. Families should ask about middle school programming, extracurricular activities, sports, and eighth-grade transition support to high school. Tobin is a solid K–8 neighborhood school option for families in Roxbury's Smith Street and Mission Hill corridors.

schools.name: Madison Park High
special_programs: Chapter 74 vocational programs (trades, technology, culinary arts, cosmetology, automotive, etc.)
schools.admissions: Citywide. Chapter 74 programs have separate competitive admissions. Non-Chapter-74 general program is open enrollment.
schools.operational_notes: Largest technical vocational high school in BPS. Chapter 74 programs produce industry credentials.
schools.summary: Madison Park Technical Vocational High School is the premier Career and Technical Education (CTE) high school in BPS and one of the most distinctive high schools in the city. Located on Malcolm X Boulevard in Roxbury, Madison Park offers state-approved Chapter 74 vocational programs — meaning students who complete them earn state-recognized industry credentials alongside their high school diplomas. Programs span carpentry, electrical technology, cosmetology, culinary arts, automotive technology, healthcare, and more. Chapter 74 programs are competitive and have their own admissions process; students interested in a specific vocational track should apply to that program specifically during BPS enrollment. The school also maintains a general academic program for students not in Chapter 74 tracks. Madison Park is citywide and open to all Boston residents, serving approximately 1,200 students. Vocational-technical education here can dramatically accelerate post-secondary employment outcomes, and many students leave with industry certifications that reduce the need for costly post-secondary training. For families with hands-on learners, students with a specific trade interest, or students who want a practical, career-connected education, Madison Park is one of the most valuable options in BPS.

schools.name: O'Bryant Math & Sci.
schools.admissions: Exam school. Admission primarily at grades 7 and 9. Unique grade 10 entry opportunity also available. MAP Growth test and minimum B GPA required.
schools.operational_notes: The only BPS exam school with a grade 10 admission opportunity.
schools.summary: John D. O'Bryant School of Mathematics and Science is one of three BPS exam schools and the most STEM-focused of the three. Named for John D. O'Bryant, the first African-American elected to the Boston School Committee, the school serves grades 7–12 with approximately 1,400 students. O'Bryant uniquely accepts a small number of new students at grade 10 in addition to standard grade 7 and 9 entry points — a rare second chance for students who did not qualify earlier but have since strengthened their academic record. The school has a strong mathematics and science curriculum with robust AP offerings in STEM subjects. Located on Malcolm X Boulevard adjacent to Madison Park High, it is accessible by MBTA Orange Line. O'Bryant consistently enrolls the most racially and socioeconomically diverse student body among the three exam schools, with a large proportion of Black and Latino students. For STEM-passionate students who want exam school rigor with a science and mathematics emphasis, O'Bryant is an outstanding choice. Families should have students take MAP Growth in grade 6 (and maintain strong grades) for grade 7 or 9 admission, or continue strengthening their record through grade 9 for possible grade 10 consideration.

schools.name: Boston Evening Academy
special_programs: Evening schedule for over-age and working students
schools.admissions: For students who are over-age, disconnected from traditional schooling, or have significant work or family obligations. Contact BPS.
schools.operational_notes: Evening schedule. Not a traditional daytime school.
schools.summary: Boston Day and Evening Academy is an alternative school serving students in grades 9–12 who need a nontraditional pathway to a high school diploma. Operating on an evening schedule, the school is designed for students who are over-age for their grade, have been disconnected from traditional schooling due to work, family, or other circumstances, or who need a more flexible approach to earning their diploma than a standard daytime school provides. The school's competency-based model allows students to progress at their own pace, which is particularly beneficial for students with complex life situations. Boston Evening Academy is a critical safety net in BPS, providing a pathway back to education for young people who might otherwise leave without a diploma. For families with older teens who have struggled in traditional settings, dropped out, or who need to work during school hours, this school represents a legitimate and supportive option for credential completion. It is not appropriate for families seeking standard daytime education for minor children entering high school from middle school in the normal timeline.

schools.name: Carter Center
schools.admissions: Specialized placement — contact BPS Office of Enrollment and BPS Specialized Services.
schools.operational_notes: Verify current grade span and program focus directly with BPS.
schools.summary: Carter Center (Carter Development Center) is a specialized BPS school in Roxbury providing programming for students with particular educational needs. The school operates under BPS's specialized services framework and serves students whose needs may not be fully met by a traditional school setting. Families are unlikely to encounter Carter Center through the standard home-based enrollment process; placement is typically coordinated through BPS's Office of Specialized Services and involves an assessment process. Parents of children with complex special education needs, significant developmental challenges, or who require a specialized smaller environment should contact BPS's specialized services office for more information. Carter Center is an important part of BPS's commitment to providing appropriate education to all students, including those with the most significant needs. Families who believe their child may require placement here should ensure their child has a current and complete IEP and should engage proactively with BPS's Child Find and specialized services teams. All specialized placements are individualized and guided by the student's IEP.

schools.name: Greater Egleston High
schools.admissions: Citywide pilot school. Apply during BPS priority registration.
schools.summary: Greater Egleston High School is a BPS pilot high school in Roxbury serving grades 9–12, explicitly designed around a smaller learning community model that prioritizes personalized relationships between students and teachers. With approximately 200 students, it is one of the smaller high schools in BPS — a deliberate design choice ensuring every student is known by name and struggles do not go unnoticed. As a pilot school, Greater Egleston has autonomy over curriculum, staffing, and school culture, allowing it to pursue instructional models that traditional BPS schools cannot easily replicate. The school serves a diverse, predominantly African-American and Latino student body from Roxbury and citywide. All Boston residents may apply as a citywide pilot. Families should visit the school, speak with current students and teachers, and ask about graduation rates, college and career outcomes, course offerings, and extracurricular programming. Greater Egleston is a strong option for students who have not thrived in larger school environments and who would benefit from the close, supportive community a smaller school provides.

schools.name: Higginson Elementary
schools.operational_notes: Distinct from Higginson/Lewis K–8 at 131 Walnut Avenue — different school, different address.
schools.summary: Higginson Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roxbury, located on Harrishof Street. Families must note that this is a distinct school from the similarly named Higginson/Lewis K–8 School at 131 Walnut Avenue — these are two separate schools with different addresses, grade configurations, and programs. Higginson Elementary serves Roxbury's diverse community with a standard elementary curriculum, following BPS's home-based assignment plan with Roxbury geographic priority. Full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats are provided. When submitting BPS enrollment forms, families should verify they are applying to the correct Higginson school (Elementary vs. Lewis K–8). For families in the Harrishof Street and adjacent Roxbury neighborhoods, Higginson Elementary is the local neighborhood elementary option.

schools.name: Dudley Street Neighborhood Charter School
schools.admissions: Citywide Horace Mann Charter. Apply during BPS enrollment period. Lottery when oversubscribed.
schools.summary: Dudley Street Neighborhood Charter School is a Horace Mann Charter School — a BPS-funded in-district charter — serving pre-kindergarten through grade 8 in Roxbury. The school's identity is deeply rooted in the Dudley Street neighborhood, one of Boston's most historically significant communities and a center of grassroots urban revitalization. The school's community-centered model emphasizes place-based education, family and community partnership, and a genuine connection to the neighborhood's history and aspirations. As a Horace Mann Charter, it operates with greater autonomy than traditional BPS schools but remains part of the BPS system, free to all enrolled students, and funded by BPS. Project-based and inquiry-driven instruction engages students in relevant, community-connected learning. The K–8 configuration allows students to remain in this distinctive community through middle school. All Boston residents may apply; a lottery is held when oversubscribed. Families should attend an information session and submit an application during BPS enrollment. Dudley Street Neighborhood Charter is an excellent option for Roxbury families who want a community-rooted, culturally connected school with an innovative instructional model.

schools.name: Perkins Elementary
schools.summary: Perkins Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in South Boston's City Point area. The school serves South Boston's community with a standard elementary curriculum in a neighborhood that has become increasingly diverse and sought-after over the past decade. South Boston has a strong community identity and active parent involvement in schools, qualities that typically translate into higher family engagement at the school level. Perkins provides full-day K2 programming and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for South Boston residents. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and student support services. For South Boston families in the City Point area, Perkins Elementary is the natural neighborhood elementary choice.

schools.name: Excel High
schools.admissions: Citywide — all Boston residents may apply.
schools.operational_notes: IMPORTANT: BPS has announced formal closure proceedings for Excel High School. Verify current operating status before applying or planning long-term enrollment here.
schools.summary: Excel High School is a citywide BPS high school serving grades 9–12 in South Boston. Families considering Excel High must be aware of a critical operational note: BPS has announced formal closure proceedings for this school, and its future is uncertain. Before making any enrollment decisions based on Excel High, families must verify the school's current operating status directly with BPS at bostonpublicschools.org or by contacting BPS's Office of Enrollment. A school under active closure proceedings should not be the centerpiece of any family's high school plan without confirmed current status. If currently enrolled families are at Excel High, they should proactively seek transition planning support from BPS, which is obligated to provide support during any closure process. Families needing a confirmed high school placement should use BPS's home-based assignment tool and explore the full range of open, operating BPS high school options.

schools.name: Tynan Elementary
schools.address: 650 E. Fourth Street, South Boston, MA 02127
schools.summary: Tynan Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in South Boston's East Side, located on East Fourth Street. The school serves a South Boston community with a strong neighborhood identity and growing diversity. It provides a standard elementary curriculum with full-day K2 programming and limited K0/K1 pre-K seats. South Boston families receive geographic priority under BPS's home-based assignment plan. The school benefits from South Boston's active community engagement culture, and family participation tends to be high. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, extracurricular offerings, and English Learner services. Tynan Elementary is the local neighborhood elementary choice for South Boston families in the East Fourth Street area.

schools.name: Perry K-8
schools.address: 745 E. Seventh Street, South Boston, MA 02127
schools.summary: Perry K–8 School serves pre-kindergarten through grade 8 in South Boston's East Side, located on East Seventh Street. As a K–8, Perry offers the significant advantage of school continuity — students complete elementary and middle school in the same building, maintaining long-term relationships with teachers and classmates and avoiding a separate middle school application. With approximately 410 students, Perry is mid-sized — large enough to offer meaningful programming but small enough to maintain community cohesion. South Boston has strong community bonds and active parent involvement, qualities that show up in Perry's school culture. The school provides full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for South Boston residents. Families should ask about middle school electives, sports and extracurricular programs, eighth-grade high school transition planning, and after-school care. For South Boston families who want K–8 continuity in a community-connected school, Perry K–8 is a strong neighborhood option.

schools.name: Middle School Academy
schools.admissions: Verify current enrollment status with BPS before applying.
schools.operational_notes: Small alternative program at the Gavin building. Co-located with UP Academy. Verify current status.
schools.summary: Middle School Academy is an alternative middle school program at the Gavin building on Dorchester Street in South Boston, co-located with UP Academy Charter School of Boston. As a smaller, alternative-model program, it serves students in grades 6–8 who may benefit from a different instructional approach or environment than a traditional middle school provides. Families should be aware that alternative programs in BPS can change in structure, enrollment capacity, and grade configuration from year to year. Before applying, families should contact BPS's Office of Enrollment directly to confirm that Middle School Academy is currently accepting general enrollment applications, what the current grade span is, and what distinguishes its instructional model from traditional BPS middle schools. The program may be particularly suited for students who have not thrived in traditional settings and who need a smaller, more personalized environment. Families seeking a confirmed standard middle school should also explore traditional BPS middle schools through the home-based assignment tool.

schools.name: UP Academy
schools.admissions: Citywide Horace Mann Charter. Apply during BPS enrollment period. Lottery when oversubscribed.
schools.summary: UP Academy Charter School of Boston is a Horace Mann Charter School — a BPS-funded in-district charter — serving grades K–8 at the Gavin building in South Boston. Part of the UP Education Network, the school is known for a structured, high-expectations instructional model that emphasizes extended learning time, strong classroom culture, and data-driven instruction — a model that has produced strong academic results particularly in literacy and mathematics. As a Horace Mann Charter, the school is tuition-free and funded by BPS but operates with significant autonomy. All Boston residents may apply, with a lottery when oversubscribed. The K–8 configuration provides continuity from kindergarten through eighth grade. Families considering UP Academy should attend an information session, understand the school's behavioral expectations and instructional model, and ask about academic outcomes, extracurricular offerings, and family engagement expectations. UP Academy South Boston is a strong option for families across the city who want a structured, high-expectations K–8 environment within the BPS system.

schools.name: Condon Elementary
schools.summary: Condon Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in South Boston, located on D Street. The school serves South Boston's increasingly diverse community with a standard elementary curriculum and community-focused culture. South Boston schools benefit from an engaged parent community and a neighborhood that has invested heavily in its public institutions. Condon provides full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for South Boston residents. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care availability, enrichment activities, and family engagement opportunities. Condon Elementary is the neighborhood school option for South Boston families in the D Street and Lower End area.

schools.name: Clap Elementary
schools.operational_notes: BPS capital planning references merger of Clap and Winthrop Elementary into the Lilla G. Frederick Elementary School. Verify current operating status before applying.
schools.summary: Roger Clap Innovation School (Clap Elementary) serves pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Dorchester. Families considering Clap must be aware of an important operational note: BPS capital planning documents announce a merger of Clap Elementary and Winthrop Elementary into a newly named school — the Lilla G. Frederick Elementary School. This merger may be in process or completed depending on the current school year. Families must verify directly with BPS whether Clap is still operating as a standalone school or has merged into Lilla G. Frederick, and what the enrollment implications are. If operating normally, Clap serves the Savin Hill and surrounding Dorchester neighborhoods with a standard elementary curriculum and follows BPS's home-based assignment plan with Dorchester geographic priority. Regardless of merger status, families in this part of Dorchester will be served by the resulting school entity and should contact BPS enrollment for current information.

schools.name: Russell Elementary
schools.summary: Russell Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Dorchester, located on Columbia Road. The school serves Dorchester's diverse community — one of Boston's largest neighborhoods, with a rich mix of African-American, Latino, Caribbean, and immigrant families. Russell provides a standard elementary curriculum with full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats. Assignment follows BPS's home-based plan with Dorchester geographic priority. The Columbia Road location is on a major Dorchester thoroughfare with good bus access. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and English Learner services. Russell Elementary is a neighborhood elementary option for families in the Columbia Road area of Dorchester.

schools.name: Trotter K-8
special_programs: Special Olympics National Banner Unified Champion School 2024–2025
schools.operational_notes: Named Special Olympics National Banner Unified Champion School 2024–2025.
schools.summary: William Monroe Trotter K–8 School in Dorchester was honored as a Special Olympics National Banner Unified Champion School for 2024–2025, one of a small number of BPS schools to earn this prestigious national recognition. Named after William Monroe Trotter, the pioneering Boston civil rights activist, the school carries a legacy of community pride and aspiration. The Special Olympics recognition reflects outstanding work integrating students with and without disabilities into shared athletic programs and school activities — a genuine inclusion culture. As a K–8, Trotter allows students to complete elementary and middle school in one building, building stable long-term community relationships. With approximately 420 students, it serves Dorchester's predominantly African-American community. Home-based assignment gives Dorchester residents geographic priority. Families should ask about athletic offerings, extracurricular activities, available special education services, and eighth-grade high school transition support. Trotter K–8 is a particularly strong recommendation for families with children who have disabilities or who value inclusive sports and community.

schools.name: King K-8
special_programs: Recipient of 2024 BPS mental health initiative ($21M)
schools.operational_notes: Identified in 2024 as part of Mayor Wu's $21M mental health initiative.
schools.summary: Martin Luther King Jr. K–8 School in Dorchester serves kindergarten through grade 8 with approximately 400 students. Named for the civil rights leader, the school was among seven BPS schools selected in 2024 by Mayor Michelle Wu's administration to receive dedicated support through a $21 million mental health initiative — meaning students have access to enhanced mental health services, counseling support, and social-emotional programming. This investment reflects both community need and recognition of the school's importance in the Dorchester ecosystem. The K–8 model allows students to remain in one school from kindergarten through eighth grade, building stable long-term community bonds. Dorchester residents receive home-based priority. Families should ask about available mental health services, academic programs, extracurricular activities, and eighth-grade high school transition planning. King K–8 is a community-anchored school actively investing in student wellbeing alongside academic achievement.

schools.name: Frederick Pilot Middle
special_programs: Pilot school curriculum and staffing autonomy
schools.admissions: Pilot school — home-based assignment with pilot lottery for grade 6.
schools.operational_notes: Also called Lilla G. Frederick Pilot Middle School. Distinct from the Lilla G. Frederick Elementary School (Clap-Winthrop merger).
schools.summary: Lilla G. Frederick Pilot Middle School is a BPS pilot school serving grades 6–8 in Dorchester. As a pilot, Frederick has meaningful autonomy over curriculum, staffing, budget, and school culture — freedoms that allow it to pursue innovative instructional approaches that traditional BPS middle schools cannot easily replicate. Named for Lilla G. Frederick, a prominent Black Boston educator, the school serves approximately 300 students in the Dorchester community. Families should note that this school is distinct from the newly forming Lilla G. Frederick Elementary School being created through the Clap-Winthrop merger — these are two separate schools sharing a similar name. As a pilot school, Frederick participates in a lottery-based enrollment process during BPS priority registration. Families should attend the school's information session and apply during January–February for grade 6. Ask about the specific instructional model, extracurricular offerings, sports, and high school transition planning. Frederick Pilot Middle is a solid middle school option for Dorchester families who want pilot school innovation without leaving BPS.

schools.name: Holland Elementary
schools.summary: Holland Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Dorchester, located on Olney Street. The school serves Dorchester's diverse community — encompassing African-American, Latino, Caribbean, and immigrant families — with a standard elementary curriculum and community-focused approach. Full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats are available, with home-based assignment priority for Dorchester residents. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and English Learner support services. Holland Elementary is the neighborhood elementary option for Dorchester families in the Olney Street area.

schools.name: Winthrop Elementary
schools.operational_notes: BPS capital planning references merger with Clap Elementary into Lilla G. Frederick Elementary School. Verify current status before applying.
schools.summary: Winthrop Elementary School serves pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Dorchester. Families considering Winthrop must be aware of an important note: BPS capital planning documents announce that Winthrop and Clap Elementary are merging into a new school called Lilla G. Frederick Elementary School. Depending on timing, Winthrop may have already merged or the process may be underway. Families must verify the current operating status of Winthrop directly with BPS before submitting enrollment applications. If still operating as Winthrop, the school serves Dorchester's Savin Hill and lower Columbia Road communities with a standard elementary curriculum and home-based assignment priority for Dorchester residents. Regardless of merger status, families in this part of Dorchester will continue to be served by the resulting school entity, and enrollment will follow standard BPS processes. Contact BPS's Office of Enrollment for current information.

schools.name: Mather Elementary
schools.operational_notes: Nation's first public elementary school (established 1639).
schools.summary: The Mather School holds a singular distinction in American educational history: it is the nation's first public elementary school, established in 1639 — a full 14 years before the founding of Boston Latin School and nearly four centuries before the modern public education system took shape. For families who value historical significance, the Mather School carries a legacy that no other elementary school in the country can match. Today, the Mather serves pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Dorchester's Neponset neighborhood with approximately 290 students, providing a standard BPS elementary curriculum in a community-centered environment. Despite its historic name, the Mather operates as a neighborhood school serving Dorchester's diverse community including Caribbean, African-American, and immigrant families. Assignment follows BPS's home-based plan with Dorchester geographic priority. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment, and family engagement. Whether you value the Mather's remarkable history or simply want a solid neighborhood elementary in lower Dorchester, it offers a meaningful educational option.

schools.name: UP Academy Charter School of Dorchester
schools.admissions: Citywide Horace Mann Charter. Apply during BPS enrollment period. Lottery when oversubscribed.
schools.summary: UP Academy Charter School of Dorchester is a Horace Mann Charter School — a BPS-funded in-district charter — serving grades K–8 at the Marshall building in Dorchester. Part of the UP Education Network, the school is characterized by extended school days, a strong culture of academic excellence, data-driven instruction, and structured behavioral expectations — a model that has produced strong academic results particularly in literacy and mathematics. As a Horace Mann Charter, the school is tuition-free and funded by BPS but operates with significant autonomy. Any Boston resident may apply through the BPS enrollment process; a lottery is held when oversubscribed.
