With approximately 500 students in a K–8 configuration, students can remain from kindergarten through eighth grade. Families should attend an information session, understand the UP Network model, and ask about academic outcomes, extracurricular programming, and high school transition planning. UP Academy Dorchester is one of the strongest K–8 options in Dorchester for families seeking a structured, high-expectations academic environment.

schools.name: Henderson Lower (K-3)
special_programs: Full inclusion for students with and without disabilities
schools.admissions: Home-based assignment. Students with IEPs may be placed through BPS Specialized Services. Verify current grade span — school has undergone reconfiguration.
schools.operational_notes: Part of Dr. William W. Henderson K–12 Inclusion School. Grade reconfiguration in recent years.
schools.summary: Henderson Lower School is the early childhood and primary division of the Dr. William W. Henderson K–12 Inclusion School — one of the most distinctive and important schools in the BPS portfolio. The Henderson is BPS's flagship inclusion school, where students with and without disabilities learn together in fully inclusive classrooms from the earliest grades through post-secondary transition. This is not mere mainstreaming: the Henderson is built around the inclusion philosophy, with co-teaching, specialized support staff, and an environment explicitly designed so that every student's disability is a natural part of the school community rather than something hidden or segregated. Henderson Lower currently serves kindergarten through grade 3 at the Dorchester Avenue building following a BPS-directed grade reconfiguration. For families of children with disabilities, the Henderson Inclusion School is often described as transformative — a school where their child is genuinely welcomed, expected to achieve, and surrounded by an accepting peer community from the start. For families of children without disabilities, Henderson offers the documented social and empathy benefits of inclusion education. Families should verify the current grade span at Henderson Lower (reconfiguration has occurred) and contact BPS Specialized Services for IEP-based placements.

schools.name: Henderson Upper (4-12)
special_programs: Full inclusion for students with and without disabilities
Recipient of 2024 BPS mental health initiative ($21M)
schools.admissions: Home-based assignment and/or IEP-based placement through BPS Specialized Services.
schools.operational_notes: Upper division of Henderson K–12 Inclusion School. Serves through post-secondary Transition (ages up to 22). 2024 mental health initiative recipient.
schools.summary: Henderson Upper School is the upper division of the Dr. William W. Henderson K–12 Inclusion School, serving grades 4–12 and a post-secondary Transition program for students up to age 22. Together with Henderson Lower, it forms one of the few true K–12 inclusion schools in Massachusetts — a place where students with and without disabilities learn side by side across all grades and subjects. The inclusion model is comprehensive: students with disabilities are full members of the school community participating in general education classes with appropriate supports, not pulled out or segregated. Research consistently shows students with disabilities achieve at higher levels in inclusive settings, while students without disabilities develop stronger empathy, communication, and collaboration skills. The Transition program serves students with disabilities beyond grade 12, providing vocational training, life skills instruction, and supported employment preparation — a critical service for families navigating post-secondary planning for students with significant disabilities. Henderson Upper was also identified for the 2024 mental health initiative, providing enhanced counseling and social-emotional resources. For any family with a child who has an IEP or disability, Henderson Upper is among the most important schools in BPS to research. Placement is coordinated through BPS Specialized Services in conjunction with the family's IEP team.

schools.name: Murphy K-8
schools.summary: Richard J. Murphy K–8 School serves kindergarten through grade 8 in Dorchester, providing a full elementary and middle school pathway within one building. With approximately 380 students, Murphy is a mid-sized K–8 that offers the community stability of a single-school journey from kindergarten through eighth grade. Located on Worrell Street in lower Dorchester, the school serves a diverse neighborhood community with African-American, Caribbean, Latino, and immigrant families. The K–8 configuration allows Murphy to build a tight-knit school culture where older students mentor younger ones and family relationships span years. Home-based assignment gives Dorchester residents priority. Families should ask about middle school programming, available electives, sports and extracurriculars, after-school care, and eighth-grade high school transition support. Murphy K–8 is a solid neighborhood option for Dorchester families who want K–8 continuity in a community-connected school.

schools.name: Kenny Elementary
schools.summary: Kenny Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Dorchester, located on Oakton Avenue. The school serves the immediate neighborhood community with a standard elementary curriculum and community-centered approach. Kenny provides full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for Dorchester residents. The school serves Dorchester's diverse population including Caribbean, African-American, and immigrant families, and provides English Learner support alongside the core curriculum. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and family engagement. Kenny Elementary is the local neighborhood elementary option for families in the Oakton Avenue area of lower Dorchester.

schools.name: Boston International HS
schools.school_type: Traditional district school (citywide, specialized for English Learners)
schools.admissions: Citywide. Designed for students not yet proficient in English. Contact BPS Welcome Center or multilingual office for referral.
schools.operational_notes: Co-located with Newcomers Academy at the Thompson building.
schools.summary: Boston International High School (BIHS) is a specialized citywide high school serving grades 9–12 exclusively for students who are not yet proficient in English — primarily recent immigrants and students new to the United States. It is one of the most important schools in BPS for newly arrived families. BIHS provides intensive English language development alongside academic instruction in core subjects, with teachers specifically trained to support English Learners at the secondary level. The school's multilingual environment — students come from dozens of countries and speak scores of languages — creates a uniquely international community where being a newcomer is the norm, not the exception. This is particularly valuable for recently arrived students who might feel isolated in a mainstream high school. BIHS also provides social-emotional support and community service referrals for students navigating the challenges of immigration. The school co-locates with the Newcomers Academy, which provides initial intensive English support. For families who have recently arrived in Boston with high school-aged students not yet proficient in English, BIHS is the most appropriate and supportive entry point into BPS secondary education.

schools.name: Newcomers Academy
special_programs: Intensive English language immersion for newly arrived immigrants
Bridge to mainstream BPS high school
schools.admissions: For recent immigrant students with limited or no English. Referral through BPS Welcome Centers.
schools.operational_notes: Co-located with Boston International High School at the Thompson building.
schools.summary: Newcomers Academy is a specialized BPS program co-located with Boston International High School at the Thompson building in Dorchester. It provides intensive English language instruction and cultural orientation for students who are recent immigrants with very limited or no English proficiency. The Academy serves as a bridge: students typically spend time in Newcomers before transitioning to Boston International High School or, depending on proficiency level, to a mainstream BPS high school. Trained English Learner educators deliver instruction, and the peer community of fellow newcomers reduces the social and cultural shock of entering a new country and school system. The program also connects students and families to community resources, legal services, and social-emotional support. Newly arrived families with high school-aged students who have limited English proficiency should contact a BPS Welcome Center — located in multiple neighborhoods across Boston — to initiate enrollment. Welcome Center staff will assess language proficiency and determine the appropriate first placement. Newcomers Academy is a critical gateway into BPS for the most recently arrived immigrant families.

schools.name: TechBoston Academy
special_programs: Recipient of 2024 BPS mental health initiative ($21M)
schools.admissions: Home-based for grades 6–8; citywide for grades 9–12.

schools.summary: TechBoston Academy is a grades 6–12 school in Dorchester with a strong technology and STEM focus, one of the few BPS schools where middle and high school students can pursue a coherent technology pathway from sixth grade through graduation. The school integrates computer science, digital literacy, engineering, and applied technology alongside traditional academic subjects. TechBoston also hosts a Haitian Creole Sheltered English Immersion program — one of only four in BPS — providing critical language support for Dorchester's large Haitian-American community. The school was identified as a 2024 mental health initiative recipient, meaning students have access to enhanced counseling and social-emotional support. TechBoston's 6–12 structure allows students who enter in middle school to develop multi-year technology projects, deepening expertise over time. The CSV also lists a 'TechBoston Acad Lower (6–9)' entry at the same address, suggesting a distinct lower-school division; families should clarify the current organizational structure when visiting. For Dorchester families — particularly those from the Haitian-American community or with technology-interested students — TechBoston Academy is a distinctive and valuable choice.

schools.name: TechBoston Acad Lower (6-9)
schools.operational_notes: Lower division of TechBoston Academy at same building.
schools.summary: TechBoston Academy Lower School is the lower division (grades 6–9) of TechBoston Academy, co-located at the same Peacevale Road building in Dorchester. It shares TechBoston's STEM and technology focus and Haitian Creole SEI program, providing continuity from middle school entry through the early high school years. The lower school allows students to begin building technology skills in grade 6 within a dedicated learning community before advancing to the full TechBoston program. Assignment is home-based for middle school grades. Families interested in TechBoston's technology pathway should contact the school directly to understand the relationship between the lower and upper school divisions and how students progress through the 6–12 program. The presence of both a lower and upper school listing at the same address reflects an organizational division that families should clarify before enrolling.

schools.name: Lee Elementary
special_programs: Recipient of 2024 BPS mental health initiative ($21M)
schools.operational_notes: Identified in 2024 as part of Mayor Wu's $21M mental health initiative.
schools.summary: Lee K–8 School serves kindergarten through grade 8 in Dorchester and was identified in 2024 as one of seven BPS schools to receive dedicated funding through Mayor Michelle Wu's $21 million youth mental health initiative. This investment significantly enhances the school's capacity to support student wellbeing through on-site counseling, mental health programming, and social-emotional learning resources. The K–8 model allows students to complete elementary and middle school years in one building, building the stable long-term community relationships that support both academic achievement and social-emotional wellbeing. The school serves Dorchester's diverse community from Talbot Avenue, with home-based assignment priority for Dorchester residents. Families should ask about the specific mental health and counseling services available, academic programs, extracurricular offerings, and eighth-grade high school transition support. Lee K–8 is a particularly strong option for families who prioritize mental health support and social-emotional programming alongside academic quality.

schools.name: Holmes Elementary

Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and family engagement. Holmes Elementary is the neighborhood elementary option for Dorchester families in the School Street area.

Families must be aware of a critical operational note: BPS has announced formal closure proceedings for CASH. Before making any enrollment decisions, families must verify the school's current status directly with BPS. CASH's Haitian Creole SEI program has been an important resource for Dorchester's Haitian-American community; families with eligible students in this language group should also ask about whether the SEI program will be maintained or transferred to another school. Families currently enrolled at CASH should seek transition planning support from BPS. For all other families planning high school enrollment, CASH should not be relied upon for long-term planning without confirmed operating status. The program at 11 Charles Street also houses Dorchester Academy, an alternative high school program at the same building.

schools.name: Dorchester Academy
special_programs: Alternative high school credit recovery and re-engagement
schools.admissions: Alternative placement — contact BPS for eligibility and referral.

schools.summary: Dorchester Academy is an alternative high school program at the Cleveland building in Dorchester, co-located with Community Academy of Science and Health. As an alternative program, it serves high school students who need a different educational setting — typically students who are over-age, have credit deficiencies, or need a more flexible, supportive structure to complete their diploma. The program focuses on credit recovery, re-engagement with education, and personalized pathways to graduation. Alternative programs like Dorchester Academy are critical in BPS, providing a supportive pathway for students who might otherwise leave without a credential. Families with students who are struggling in traditional high school settings, who have missed significant time, or who are significantly behind in credits should contact BPS enrollment to determine whether Dorchester Academy or another alternative program is an appropriate option. This program is not accessed through standard home-based enrollment; placement involves a referral and assessment process through BPS.

schools.name: P.A. Shaw
schools.summary: P.A. Shaw Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Dorchester, located on Norfolk Street. The school serves the surrounding Dorchester community with a standard elementary curriculum and a focus on family engagement and community partnership. P.A. Shaw provides full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for Dorchester residents. The school serves Dorchester's diverse population including African-American, Caribbean, Latino, and immigrant families. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and English Learner support services. P.A. Shaw is the neighborhood elementary option for families in the Norfolk Street and surrounding Dorchester areas.

schools.name: Greenwood Sarah K-8
schools.summary: Sarah Greenwood K–8 School serves kindergarten through grade 8 in Dorchester, providing elementary and middle school continuity for the local community. Named for Sarah Greenwood, a pioneering Boston educator who served for decades in the 19th century, the school carries a legacy of educational commitment. The K–8 configuration allows students to remain in one school from kindergarten through eighth grade, building long-term community bonds and avoiding a separate middle school application. The school serves Dorchester's diverse community with approximately 370 students and follows BPS's home-based assignment plan. Families should ask about middle school programming, extracurricular offerings, sports, and eighth-grade high school transition support. Sarah Greenwood K–8 is a solid neighborhood K–8 option for Dorchester families in the Glenway Street area.

schools.name: Burke High
schools.admissions: Citywide — all Boston residents may apply.
schools.operational_notes: Shares building with Dearborn STEM Academy. Also known as Jeremiah E. Burke High School.
schools.summary: Jeremiah E. Burke High School is a comprehensive citywide high school serving grades 9–12 in Dorchester with approximately 800 students, and one of only three BPS schools hosting a Cape Verdean Creole Sheltered English Immersion program. For Cape Verdean-speaking families with high school-aged students who need English Learner support, Burke is one of the very few options in BPS that provides Cape Verdean Creole SEI at the secondary level — a critical resource given Boston's large Cape Verdean community, especially in Dorchester. Beyond the SEI program, Burke offers Career and Technical Education pathways. The school shares its Washington Street building with Dearborn STEM Academy, creating a multi-school campus. All BPS high schools are citywide, so any Boston resident may apply. Families should ask about AP and advanced course offerings, graduation and college acceptance rates, CTE pathway options, extracurricular programs, and English Learner support. For the Cape Verdean community and Dorchester families generally, Burke High is a significant and accessible comprehensive high school option.

schools.name: Dearborn Middle School
schools.admissions: Home-based for grades 6–8; citywide for grades 9–12.
schools.operational_notes: Full name: Dearborn STEM Academy. Co-located with Burke High at Washington Street.
schools.summary: Dearborn STEM Academy is a grades 6–12 school in Dorchester with a STEM-focused curriculum and a Cape Verdean Creole SEI program — one of only three in BPS. Co-located with Jeremiah E. Burke High School at 60 Washington Street, Dearborn provides a coherent STEM pathway from middle school through high school, enabling students who enter in grade 6 to develop multi-year science, technology, engineering, and mathematics projects and expertise. The Cape Verdean Creole SEI program makes Dearborn one of a small number of schools offering both specialized STEM academics and language support for Cape Verdean students — a rare combination. For Dorchester families with STEM-interested students, or for the Cape Verdean community seeking a school with both Creole SEI and specialized academics, Dearborn STEM Academy is one of the most compelling options in the district. Families should apply during priority BPS registration for grade 6; high school students may apply as a citywide option.

Dorchester families seeking a confirmed middle school placement should use BPS's home-based assignment tool and contact the Office of Enrollment for current information.

schools.name: Everett Elementary
schools.summary: Everett Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Dorchester, located on Pleasant Street. The school serves lower Dorchester's community with a standard elementary curriculum and community-focused approach. Full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats are available, with home-based assignment priority for Dorchester residents. The school serves a diverse student population including African-American, Caribbean, and immigrant families and provides English Learner support. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care availability, enrichment activities, and family engagement. Everett Elementary is a neighborhood option for Dorchester families in the Pleasant Street and lower Dorchester corridor.

schools.name: Taylor Elementary
schools.admissions: Home-based assignment. Haitian Creole SEI program may have citywide access for eligible families.
schools.operational_notes: One of four BPS schools with Haitian Creole SEI.
schools.summary: Taylor Elementary School in Mattapan hosts one of only four Haitian Creole Sheltered English Immersion programs in all of BPS — a critically important resource for Mattapan's large Haitian-American community, one of the highest concentrations of Haitian-American families in New England. The Haitian Creole SEI program provides children from these families with native-language academic support while they develop English proficiency, an approach research consistently shows accelerates both language acquisition and long-term academic achievement. For Haitian Creole-speaking families with elementary-aged children, Taylor is often the most appropriate and culturally responsive school in BPS for their community. Beyond the SEI program, Taylor serves approximately 310 students with a standard elementary curriculum and community-centered approach. Home-based assignment gives Mattapan residents geographic priority. Families should ask about the structure of the Haitian Creole SEI program, when students typically transition to mainstream English instruction, and what supports are available at each stage. For any Haitian Creole-speaking family in Boston with an elementary-aged child, Taylor Elementary should be near the top of the enrollment list.

schools.name: Mildred Avenue K-8
schools.summary: Mildred Avenue K–8 School serves kindergarten through grade 8 in Mattapan, providing elementary and middle school continuity for families in this predominantly African-American and Haitian-American neighborhood. As a K–8, Mildred Avenue allows students to remain in one building from kindergarten through eighth grade, reducing educational transitions and building long-term community bonds. The school serves approximately 360 students and reflects Mattapan's diverse community. Home-based assignment gives Mattapan residents geographic priority. Families should ask about middle school programming, extracurricular offerings, sports, after-school care, and eighth-grade high school transition planning. Mildred Avenue K–8 is a solid neighborhood K–8 option for Mattapan families who want continuity and a community-rooted school experience.

schools.summary: Young Achievers Science and Math K–8 is a BPS pilot school in Mattapan that has built a strong reputation for its science and mathematics focus at the elementary and middle school level. As a pilot school, Young Achievers has autonomy over its curriculum and instructional approach, which it uses to create a more rigorous STEM-centered learning environment than a traditional district school. The school was among seven BPS schools selected in 2024 for Mayor Wu's $21 million mental health initiative, reflecting both community need and the school's commitment to whole-child wellbeing. With approximately 420 students in a K–8 configuration, Young Achievers provides both STEM-focused academics and the continuity of a single school from kindergarten through eighth grade. The school participates in BPS's pilot school lottery during priority registration (January–February). Families should attend the information session and ask about the STEM programming at each grade level, after-school enrichment, available mental health services, extracurricular activities, and eighth-grade high school preparation. Young Achievers K–8 is one of the most compelling school options in Mattapan for families who value STEM education, pilot innovation, and strong student support.

schools.name: Mattahunt Elementary
schools.summary: Mattahunt Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Mattapan, located on Hebron Street. The school serves the immediate Mattapan community with a standard elementary curriculum and community-centered approach. Mattapan is one of Boston's most historically significant African-American communities, and Mattahunt serves a student population reflecting the neighborhood's African-American and Haitian-American families. Full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats are provided, with home-based assignment priority for Mattapan residents. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, English Learner support services, and family engagement. Mattahunt Elementary is the local neighborhood elementary option for families in the Hebron Street and surrounding Mattapan areas.

schools.name: Chittick Elementary
schools.summary: Chittick Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Mattapan, located on Ruskindale Road. The school serves the surrounding Mattapan community with a standard elementary curriculum and a focus on family engagement and academic support. Chittick serves Mattapan's predominantly African-American and Haitian-American student population and provides English Learner services alongside the core curriculum. Full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats are available, with home-based assignment priority for Mattapan residents. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and available student support services. Chittick Elementary is the neighborhood elementary option for Mattapan families in the Ruskindale Road area.

schools.name: Ellison/ Parks ELC
schools.admissions: Apply through BPS enrollment. K0/K1 seats NOT guaranteed. Most K0 seats reserved for students with disabilities.
schools.summary: Ellison/Parks Early Learning Center is a dedicated BPS early childhood center serving children ages 3 and 4 in Mattapan through K0 and K1 pre-K programs. It is one of a small number of standalone early education centers in BPS, providing focused pre-K programming before children transition to full-day kindergarten (K2) at an elementary school. The center serves Mattapan's African-American and Haitian-American community and provides a developmentally appropriate, nurturing early childhood environment. Families must understand that K0 (age 3) seats are extremely limited — most are reserved for children with identified disabilities. K1 (age 4) seats have broader availability but are still not guaranteed. Priority registration runs from January through early February; children must be 3 or 4 years old by September 1. After K1, families apply separately for K2 at an elementary school — K2 placement is guaranteed for all BPS applicants though not at a specific school. Families in Mattapan seeking early childhood education should also explore the Great Starts platform for a full picture of BPS and community childcare options.

schools.name: Philbrick Elementary

schools.summary: Philbrick Elementary School is listed in BPS records serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roslindale. Families must be aware of a significant operational note: BPS has completed or is in the process of completing a merger of Philbrick Elementary and Sumner Elementary into a new school called Sarah Roberts Elementary School. Named for Sarah Roberts, whose 1849 legal case against Boston's segregated schools is considered a landmark precursor to Brown v. Board of Education, the new school carries a historically resonant name. Depending on when you are reading this, Philbrick may no longer exist as a standalone school. Families must verify the current status directly with BPS before applying. If the merger is complete, families in this area of Roslindale should look for Sarah Roberts Elementary in BPS enrollment listings. If Philbrick is still operating independently, it provides a standard BPS elementary curriculum with home-based assignment priority for Roslindale residents.

schools.name: Haley Elementary
schools.admissions: Pilot school — home-based assignment with pilot lottery.
schools.summary: Haley K–8 Pilot School in Roslindale is a BPS pilot school serving kindergarten through grade 8 with meaningful autonomy over its curriculum, staffing, and school culture. As a pilot, Haley can pursue instructional innovations and create a distinctive school identity that traditional BPS schools cannot easily replicate. The K–8 configuration provides the valuable benefit of school continuity from kindergarten through eighth grade, allowing students to build long-term community bonds and avoiding a separate middle school application. The school is located on American Legion Highway in Roslindale and serves the surrounding neighborhood's diverse community. Pilot schools participate in a lottery enrollment process during BPS priority registration; families should apply in January–February for kindergarten or grade 6 entry. Families should attend the school's information session and ask about the specific instructional model, middle school programming, extracurricular offerings, sports, after-school care, and eighth-grade high school transition planning. For Roslindale families who want a K–8 school with pilot school flexibility in their neighborhood, Haley Pilot is a strong option.

schools.name: Conley Elementary
schools.summary: Conley Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roslindale, located on Poplar Street. The school serves Roslindale's increasingly diverse community — a neighborhood that has evolved significantly in recent decades and is now home to families of many different backgrounds including African-American, Latino, and immigrant communities. Conley provides a standard elementary curriculum with full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for Roslindale residents. The school is a neighborhood anchor offering a community-centered educational environment. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and family engagement opportunities. Conley Elementary is the local neighborhood elementary option for Roslindale families in the Poplar Street area.

schools.name: Irving Middle
schools.summary: Irving Middle School is a dedicated middle school serving grades 6–8 in Roslindale, located on Cummins Highway. Dedicated middle schools like Irving allow students to experience departmentalized instruction by subject-area teachers, expanded extracurricular offerings, and age-specific social development in a setting designed for the middle school years. For families whose children are transitioning from a K–6 elementary school in Roslindale, Irving Middle is often the natural home-based assignment destination for grade 6. The school serves Roslindale's diverse community and provides the standard BPS middle school curriculum. Home-based assignment gives Roslindale residents geographic priority. Families should ask about available electives, sports teams, extracurricular clubs, after-school programming, social-emotional support, and how the school prepares eighth-graders for the high school transition. Irving Middle is the primary traditional middle school option for Roslindale families.

schools.name: Sumner Elementary
schools.operational_notes: BPS merged Sumner and Philbrick Elementary into Sarah Roberts Elementary School for 2025–26. Verify current status.
schools.summary: Charles Sumner Elementary School is listed in BPS records serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roslindale. Families must be aware of an important note: BPS has completed or is completing a merger of Sumner Elementary and Philbrick Elementary into a new school called Sarah Roberts Elementary School. The new school is named after Sarah Roberts, whose 1849 civil rights case in Boston — a Black girl denied admission to a white school — is recognized as a legal precursor to Brown v. Board of Education, and carries a historically meaningful name honoring the struggle for equal educational access. Families should verify the current status of Sumner directly with BPS before applying. If the merger is complete, families in this area of Roslindale should look for Sarah Roberts Elementary in BPS enrollment listings. If Sumner is still operating independently, it provides a standard BPS elementary curriculum with home-based assignment priority for Roslindale residents.

schools.name: Bates Elementary
schools.summary: Bates Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roslindale, located on Beech Street. The school draws from Roslindale's increasingly diverse population, which includes African-American, Latino, immigrant, and long-established New England families. Full-day K2 is provided, and limited pre-K seats are available. Home-based assignment gives Roslindale residents geographic priority. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and available student support services. Bates Elementary is a neighborhood elementary option for Roslindale families in the Beech Street area. Families considering both Bates and Mozart Elementary should note they are both on Beech Street — the home-based assignment tool will indicate which school appears on a given family's list based on home address.

schools.name: Mozart Elementary
schools.summary: Mozart Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Roslindale on Beech Street, near Bates Elementary. Mozart provides a standard BPS elementary curriculum with full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for Roslindale residents. The school serves Roslindale's diverse community reflecting the neighborhood's African-American, Latino, immigrant, and long-established resident families. Families considering both Mozart and Bates (which are on the same street) should use BPS's home-based assignment tool to determine which school their address prioritizes. Families should ask about academic programs, enrichment offerings, after-school care, and family engagement activities. Mozart Elementary is a solid neighborhood option for Roslindale families in the Beech Street corridor.

schools.name: BTU K-8 Pilot
schools.address: 25 Walk Hill Street, Jamaica Plain, MA 02130
schools.admissions: Pilot school — home-based assignment with pilot lottery.
schools.summary: Boston Teachers Union K–8 Pilot School (BTU School) is one of the most distinctive schools in BPS — a teacher-led pilot school in Jamaica Plain where educators hold meaningful leadership authority over the school's direction, curriculum, and culture. The school operates through a shared leadership model that genuinely distributes power between teachers, families, and students, rooted in the belief that those closest to students — their teachers — are best positioned to make instructional decisions. The result is a school culture of professional investment, innovation, and accountability that is difficult to replicate in traditional structures. The school employs inquiry-based learning approaches that encourage students to ask questions and investigate rather than passively receive information. As a K–8, the BTU School provides continuity from kindergarten through eighth grade. The school serves Jamaica Plain's diverse community with approximately 350 students. As a pilot, it participates in a lottery enrollment process during BPS priority registration (January–February). Families should attend the school's information session and ask about the instructional model, middle school programming, extracurriculars, and eighth-grade transition planning. BTU K–8 is an excellent choice for families who value teacher professionalism, shared governance, and inquiry-based learning.

schools.name: Community Academy
schools.admissions: Alternative placement — verify current status with BPS.
schools.operational_notes: IMPORTANT: BPS has announced closure of Community Academy. Verify current status before making any enrollment decisions.
schools.summary: Community Academy is an alternative school in Jamaica Plain that has been announced for closure by BPS. Families must verify the current operating status of Community Academy directly with BPS before making any enrollment plans based on this school. Do not plan a child's education around a school with announced closure proceedings without first confirming it will be open and accepting students in the relevant school year. If families are currently enrolled at Community Academy, they should proactively request transition planning support from BPS, which is responsible for ensuring that students affected by school closures are supported in finding appropriate placements at operating schools. Families seeking confirmed alternative or standard educational options in the Jamaica Plain area should use BPS's home-based assignment tool and consult with an enrollment specialist at a BPS Welcome Center.

schools.name: English High
schools.admissions: Citywide — all Boston residents may apply. No exam required.
schools.operational_notes: Second oldest public high school in the United States (founded 1821).
schools.summary: The English High School holds the distinction of being the second-oldest public high school in the United States, founded in 1821. For nearly two centuries, English High has educated generations of Boston students, carrying a legacy of civic contribution and academic achievement that few schools anywhere can match. Today, it serves grades 9–12 with approximately 700 students in Jamaica Plain, operating as a citywide high school open to all Boston residents. The school reflects Jamaica Plain's diverse, multicultural community and serves students from a wide range of backgrounds and neighborhoods across the city. English High offers a comprehensive academic program with extracurricular activities and athletics; its location in Jamaica Plain near the Orange Line provides good transit access from across Boston. All BPS high schools are citywide choices. Families should ask about AP course offerings, graduation and college acceptance rates, available sports and clubs, and student support services including college advising. For families who value historical legacy, community identity, and a comprehensive citywide high school in Jamaica Plain, English High is a compelling option.

schools.name: Kennedy John F Elemen
schools.summary: John F. Kennedy Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Jamaica Plain, located on Bolster Street. The school serves Jamaica Plain's diverse and vibrant community — one of Boston's most diverse and dynamic neighborhoods with a strong community identity and progressive civic engagement culture. JFK Elementary draws students from multiple ethnic, linguistic, and economic backgrounds and provides a standard elementary curriculum with full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats. Home-based assignment gives Jamaica Plain residents priority. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, English Learner services, and family engagement opportunities. JFK Elementary is a solid neighborhood elementary choice for Jamaica Plain families.

schools.name: West Zone ELC
special_programs: Integrated early childhood classrooms for students with and without disabilities
schools.admissions: Apply through BPS enrollment. K0 primarily for students with disabilities. K1 available with limited seats.
schools.operational_notes: Shares Hennigan building with Hennigan K–8. Inclusion-focused early education.
schools.summary: West Zone Early Learning Center is a BPS early childhood center serving children ages 3 and 4 in Jamaica Plain through K0 and K1 programming, co-located at the Hennigan building with Hennigan K–8. What distinguishes West Zone ELC from other BPS early education centers is its commitment to inclusion: the school offers integrated early childhood classrooms where children with and without disabilities learn together from the youngest ages. This model is particularly valuable for families of children with identified disabilities or developmental delays who want their child in a natural, inclusive peer environment rather than a segregated special education setting. The center also provides ESL services supporting Jamaica Plain's multilingual families. For families of children with disabilities seeking early childhood inclusion, West Zone ELC is one of the few BPS early education options with this explicit focus. K0 seats are extremely limited and most are reserved for children with IEPs. K1 seats have broader availability but are still competitive. Families with children who have identified disabilities should contact BPS Specialized Services alongside the standard enrollment process. Families should also explore the Great Starts platform for other early childhood options in Jamaica Plain.

schools.name: Hennigan K-8
schools.operational_notes: Shares Hennigan building with West Zone ELC.
schools.summary: Hennigan K–8 School serves kindergarten through grade 8 in Jamaica Plain, sharing the Hennigan building on Heath Street with West Zone Early Learning Center. As a K–8, Hennigan provides educational continuity from kindergarten through eighth grade, allowing students to build long-term community bonds and avoid a separate middle school application. With approximately 420 students, the school reflects Jamaica Plain's diverse community — one of Boston's most vibrant and multicultural neighborhoods. Home-based assignment gives Jamaica Plain residents priority. Families should ask about middle school course offerings, extracurricular activities, sports, after-school care, and eighth-grade high school transition planning. Hennigan K–8 is a solid K–8 neighborhood option for Jamaica Plain families.

schools.name: Curley Lower (K1-5)
schools.operational_notes: Lower division of James J. Curley K–8 School. Students continue to Curley Upper (grades 6–8) at 493 Centre Street.
schools.summary: James J. Curley Lower School serves grades K1 through 5 in Jamaica Plain as the lower division of the James J. Curley K–8 School, which is split across two buildings. Students who complete their lower school years at Curley Lower advance to Curley Upper (grades 6–8) at a separate building on Centre Street, creating a K–8 pathway across two locations. The lower school building on Pershing Road houses the youngest Curley students in a setting scaled for early childhood and early elementary learners. Jamaica Plain's diverse community is well reflected in the Curley student body. Home-based assignment gives Jamaica Plain residents priority. K1 pre-K programming is available. Families should ask about the transition process from Curley Lower to Upper, available after-school care, enrichment activities, and family engagement. For families in the Pershing Road area of Jamaica Plain, Curley Lower is the neighborhood entry point into the Curley K–8 pathway.

schools.name: Curley Upper (6-8)
schools.admissions: Home-based assignment. Students from Curley Lower typically continue here.
schools.operational_notes: Upper division of James J. Curley K–8 School.
schools.summary: James J. Curley Upper School serves grades 6–8 in Jamaica Plain as the upper division of the Curley K–8 School. Students who complete lower school at Curley Lower (K1–5 on Pershing Road) typically continue to Curley Upper on Centre Street for middle school grades. While the two buildings are separate, the Curley name and shared community culture create continuity across the K–8 journey. The Centre Street location is in a lively part of Jamaica Plain near the Orange Line. Curley Upper provides a dedicated middle school experience for approximately 230 students with departmentalized instruction, expanded extracurriculars, and age-appropriate programming. Home-based assignment gives Jamaica Plain residents priority for grade 6 applications. Families should ask about available electives, sports teams and clubs, after-school care, social-emotional support, and how the school prepares eighth-graders for the high school transition. Curley Upper is a solid middle school option for Jamaica Plain families, particularly those already in the Curley community through Curley Lower.

schools.name: Manning Elementary
schools.summary: Manning Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Jamaica Plain, located on Louders Lane. The school serves a Jamaica Plain community that has become increasingly diverse over the past decade and is known for its active civic engagement and progressive neighborhood culture. Manning provides a standard elementary curriculum with full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for Jamaica Plain residents. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and English Learner services. Manning Elementary is a neighborhood elementary option for Jamaica Plain families in the Louders Lane area.

schools.name: Fenway High
special_programs: College credit partnerships with UMass Boston and Wentworth Institute
schools.admissions: Citywide pilot school. Apply during BPS priority registration (January–February). Information night in fall semester.
schools.operational_notes: One of BPS's most acclaimed pilot high schools. Founded 1983.
schools.summary: Fenway High School is one of the most acclaimed schools in the BPS portfolio and a nationally recognized model for small, personalized high school education. Founded in 1983 as one of BPS's first pilot schools, Fenway is a state-designated Early College High School — meaning students can earn up to two years of college credit through formal partnerships with UMass Boston and Wentworth Institute of Technology, a significant head start that can dramatically reduce the cost and time of a four-year degree. The school's educational philosophy centers on five Habits of Mind — Evidence, Viewpoint, Connections, Supposition, and Relevance — a framework for intellectual inquiry that prepares students for genuine college-level academic work and lifelong critical thinking, not just college admissions. With approximately 380 students in grades 9–12, Fenway is deliberately small, enabling teachers to know every student well and respond to individual needs. The school emphasizes active citizenship and community engagement alongside academic excellence. As a citywide pilot, Fenway draws students from across Boston and has produced graduates who attend highly selective universities. Families should attend Fenway's information night in the fall, apply during January–February priority registration, and speak with current students. For academically motivated students who want a rigorous, intellectually stimulating high school with real college coursework and a community where every student matters, Fenway High School is one of the top choices in BPS.

schools.name: Mission Hill K-8
schools.admissions: Pilot school — verify current enrollment status before applying.
schools.operational_notes: IMPORTANT: Wikipedia reports Mission Hill School (pilot) was closed by BPS in May 2022 following a bullying investigation. This address appears in 2024–2025 BPS records. Verify current operating status directly with BPS before applying.
schools.summary: Mission Hill K–8 is listed in BPS records at 20 Child Street in Jamaica Plain for the 2024–2025 school year. Families must be aware of a critical operational note: the original Mission Hill School (pilot) was voted for closure by the Boston School Committee in May 2022 following a scathing investigation into multiple bullying incidents at the school. The presence of this address in current BPS records may indicate that a different or reconstituted program is now operating at this location. Before making any enrollment decisions based on 'Mission Hill K–8,' families must contact BPS's Office of Enrollment to confirm whether this is an actively enrolling school, its current name and status, and its current leadership and culture. Do not rely on historical reputation (positive or negative) for a school that has undergone significant institutional change without first verifying the current situation. Note that this building also houses Margarita Muñiz Academy (grades 7–12), which is actively enrolling. Contact BPS enrollment for the most current information.

schools.name: Margarita Muniz Academy
schools.admissions: Citywide. Standard entry points: grades K1–2 and grades 9–11. Students entering grades 3–8 require language assessment in Spanish. Apply during BPS enrollment.
schools.operational_notes: One of a small number of BPS dual language schools.
schools.summary: Margarita Muñiz Academy is one of the most distinctive schools in BPS — a dual language school serving grades 7–12 where all students develop academic fluency in both English and Spanish. Named for pioneering Puerto Rican educator Margarita Muñiz, the school is citywide and draws students from across Boston's diverse Latino and non-Latino communities. The dual language model is not simply Spanish class: it is genuine bilingual academic instruction across all subjects, aiming for students who can read, write, analyze, and present at high academic levels in both languages. Research on dual language education consistently shows bilingual students outperform monolingual peers academically over time, and graduates who achieve biliteracy are more competitive in college admissions and the job market. Starting in grade 10, Muñiz offers Early College programming, allowing students to earn college credits during high school and significantly reducing the cost of a degree. As a dual language school, standard entry points are grades K1–2 and grades 9–11; students seeking to enter grades 3–8 require a Spanish language assessment. For Spanish-speaking families, Muñiz is one of the most compelling high school options in BPS — a school where the home language is an academic asset. For non-Spanish-speaking families, Muñiz offers a rigorous bilingual education that opens significant doors. Highly recommended for families who value bilingualism and early college access.

schools.name: Roosevelt Upper (2-7)
schools.operational_notes: Upper division of Roosevelt K–8 School. Lower division (K1–1) is at 30 Millstone Road.
schools.summary: Roosevelt Upper School serves grades 2–7 in Hyde Park at the Needham Road building as the upper division of the Roosevelt K–8 School, which is split across two buildings. Students who start at Roosevelt Lower (K1–Grade 1 at the Millstone Road building) advance here for grades 2–7. This split-building K–8 configuration is less common in BPS; families should understand both buildings are part of the same school pathway. Roosevelt Upper provides intermediate elementary and early middle school years for Hyde Park's diverse community. Home-based assignment gives Hyde Park residents priority. Families should ask about available enrichment programs and electives in the upper grades, after-school care, sports and extracurriculars, and how the school supports the eventual transition to high school. For Hyde Park families in the Roosevelt pathway, Roosevelt Upper is the primary school home for grades 2–7.

schools.name: Roosevelt K-8 (K1-1)
schools.operational_notes: Lower division of Roosevelt K–8 School. Students continue to Roosevelt Upper (grades 2–7) at Needham Road.
schools.summary: Roosevelt K–8 Lower School serves grades K1 through Grade 1 at the New Roosevelt building on Millstone Road in Hyde Park as the entry division of the Roosevelt K–8 School. Students completing Grade 1 here advance to Roosevelt Upper (grades 2–7) at the Needham Road building, creating a split-building K–8 pathway. The lower school building provides an early childhood and primary grades environment scaled for the youngest learners. Hyde Park is a diverse residential neighborhood, and the Roosevelt pathway serves local families. Home-based assignment gives Hyde Park residents priority. Families entering kindergarten (K1) should understand the transition from this building to Roosevelt Upper and ask about the enrollment process, what programs are available at both levels, and after-school care options. Roosevelt K–8 Lower is the starting point of Hyde Park's primary K–8 school pathway.

schools.name: Channing Elementary
schools.summary: Channing Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Hyde Park, located on Sunnyside Street. The school serves Hyde Park's diverse community with a standard elementary curriculum and community-focused approach. Hyde Park is one of Boston's most diverse neighborhoods with a mix of African-American, Caribbean, Latino, and long-established families. Channing provides full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats, with home-based assignment priority for Hyde Park residents. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and family engagement. Channing Elementary is a neighborhood elementary option for Hyde Park families in the Sunnyside Street area.

schools.name: Grew Elementary
schools.summary: Grew Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in Hyde Park, located on Gordon Avenue. The school serves Hyde Park's diverse community with a standard elementary curriculum and community-centered approach. Full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats are provided, with home-based assignment priority for Hyde Park residents. Hyde Park families benefit from multiple elementary school options through the home-based assignment system, and Grew is one of those neighborhood choices. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment offerings, and family engagement. Grew Elementary is the local elementary option for Hyde Park families in the Gordon Avenue area.

schools.name: New Mission High
schools.admissions: Citywide pilot school. Apply during BPS priority registration.
schools.operational_notes: Shares building with Boston Community Leadership Academy.
schools.summary: New Mission High School is a BPS pilot high school in Hyde Park serving grades 9–12. As a pilot school, New Mission has meaningful autonomy over its curriculum, staffing, and school culture, allowing it to pursue a personalized learning model that recognizes students learn best when their individual strengths, interests, and needs are known and addressed. With approximately 350 students, the school is smaller than a comprehensive high school, enabling closer student-teacher relationships and a more supportive environment. As a citywide pilot, New Mission draws students from across Boston. The school shares its building with Boston Community Leadership Academy. Pilot school enrollment involves a lottery during BPS priority registration (January–February). Families should attend the information session and ask about course offerings, graduation and college placement rates, extracurricular programs, and social-emotional support services. For students who benefit from a smaller, more personalized school environment and want pilot school innovation in Hyde Park, New Mission High is a strong option.

schools.name: Community Leadership Academy
schools.admissions: Citywide Horace Mann Charter. Apply during BPS enrollment period. Lottery when oversubscribed.
schools.operational_notes: Shares building with New Mission High. Formed through McCormack-BCLA merger (2021).
schools.summary: Boston Community Leadership Academy (BCLA) is a Horace Mann Charter School — a BPS-funded in-district charter — serving grades 6–12 in Hyde Park. BCLA was formed through a 2021 merger with John W. McCormack Middle School, and its leadership development focus reflects a school culture that cultivates leadership skills, civic responsibility, and community engagement in students from middle school through graduation — alongside rigorous academic preparation. As a Horace Mann Charter, BCLA operates with greater autonomy than a traditional BPS school but is fully funded by BPS and tuition-free to all enrolled students. The 6–12 configuration allows students to build a long-term school community through high school graduation. BCLA is citywide, open to all Boston residents, and holds a lottery when oversubscribed. Families should attend an information session and apply during BPS enrollment. For families seeking a citywide 6–12 in-district charter option with a focus on leadership development and civic engagement, Boston Community Leadership Academy is a distinctive and valuable choice.

schools.name: West Roxbury Academy
schools.admissions: Citywide — all Boston residents may apply. No exam required.
schools.operational_notes: Shares building with Urban Science Academy (pilot).
schools.summary: West Roxbury Academy is a citywide BPS high school serving grades 9–12 in West Roxbury at the V.F.W. Parkway campus, sharing the building with Urban Science Academy. The school offers a comprehensive high school education in a relatively quiet, residential area of Boston. While the V.F.W. Parkway location is accessible by bus and nearby commuter rail, transit options are more limited than in inner-city neighborhoods — families commuting from across Boston should factor this in. All BPS high schools are citywide, so any Boston family may apply. Families should ask about AP and advanced course offerings, graduation and college acceptance rates, sports and extracurricular programs, and student support services including college advising. For families in West Roxbury and across the city seeking a comprehensive citywide high school in a quieter residential setting, West Roxbury Academy is a solid option worth exploring alongside the pilot school next door.

schools.name: Urban Science Academy
schools.admissions: Citywide pilot school. Apply during BPS priority registration.
schools.operational_notes: Shares building with West Roxbury Academy.
schools.summary: Urban Science Academy is a BPS pilot high school sharing the West Roxbury Education Complex with West Roxbury Academy. As a pilot, Urban Science Academy has autonomy over curriculum, staffing, and culture, which it uses to pursue a science-focused, personalized learning model. The school's science emphasis provides students with stronger foundational STEM preparation than a typical comprehensive high school, and its smaller size (approximately 250 students) enables more individualized instruction and closer student-teacher relationships. As a citywide pilot, Urban Science Academy draws students from across Boston and is accessible to all Boston residents through the BPS enrollment process. The school participates in the pilot school lottery during priority registration (January–February). Families should attend the information session and ask about the science curriculum, AP course offerings, extracurricular programs, and college placement outcomes. For students interested in science or STEM fields who want a smaller, personalized high school experience with pilot school innovation, Urban Science Academy is compelling — even though its West Roxbury location requires a longer commute from many parts of the city.

schools.name: Kilmer Upper (4-8)
schools.operational_notes: Upper division of Kilmer K–8 School. Lower division (K1–3) is at Baker Street.
schools.summary: Kilmer K–8 Upper School serves grades 4–8 in West Roxbury at the Russett Road building as the upper division of the Kilmer K–8 School. Students completing early elementary years at Kilmer Lower (K1–3 on Baker Street) advance to Kilmer Upper for grades 4–8. The split-building structure means families navigate two physical locations within the same K–8 pathway — worth understanding clearly before enrolling. Kilmer Upper provides the intermediate elementary and middle school years, supporting students' academic and social development through the pre-adolescent and adolescent stages. West Roxbury is a largely residential neighborhood, and Kilmer serves an increasingly diverse community. Home-based assignment gives West Roxbury residents priority. Families should ask about the transition from Kilmer Lower to Upper, available enrichment and elective courses in the upper grades, sports and extracurriculars, after-school care, and eighth-grade high school transition planning.

schools.name: Kilmer Lower (K1-3)
schools.operational_notes: Lower division of Kilmer K–8 School. Upper division (grades 4–8) is at Russett Road.
schools.summary: Kilmer K–8 Lower School serves grades K1 through Grade 3 at the Baker Street building in West Roxbury as the lower division of the Kilmer K–8 School. Students entering kindergarten here will transition to Kilmer Upper (grades 4–8) at the Russett Road building after completing third grade — a split-building arrangement that is one of the less common configurations in BPS and worth understanding clearly before enrolling. The lower school provides an early childhood and primary grades environment for West Roxbury's community. Home-based assignment gives West Roxbury residents priority. Families should ask about the transition from Kilmer Lower to Upper, K1 pre-K availability, after-school care options, and enrichment in the early grades. Kilmer Lower is the neighborhood kindergarten entry point for West Roxbury families in the Kilmer pathway.

schools.name: Beethoven Elementary
schools.summary: Beethoven Elementary School is a traditional BPS neighborhood school serving pre-kindergarten through grade 6 in West Roxbury on Washington Street. The school is one of several elementary schools serving West Roxbury's residential neighborhoods and provides a standard BPS elementary curriculum with full-day K2 and limited pre-K seats. Home-based assignment gives West Roxbury residents priority. West Roxbury's demographics have become increasingly diverse in recent decades, and Beethoven serves a community reflecting that change. Families should ask about academic programs, after-school care, enrichment activities, and family engagement opportunities. Beethoven Elementary is a neighborhood option for West Roxbury families in the Washington Street corridor.

schools.name: Lyndon K-8
schools.address: 20 Mt. Vernon Street, West Roxbury, MA 02132
schools.admissions: Pilot school — home-based assignment with pilot lottery.
schools.summary: Lyndon K–8 Pilot School in West Roxbury is a BPS pilot school serving kindergarten through grade 8 with autonomy to shape its curriculum, staffing, and school culture. Pilot status gives Lyndon meaningful flexibility to pursue innovative instructional practices and create a distinctive school identity within the BPS framework. The K–8 configuration provides school continuity from kindergarten through eighth grade, avoiding a separate middle school application and building long-term community bonds. Lyndon serves approximately 350 students from West Roxbury's community. As a pilot, it participates in a lottery enrollment process during BPS priority registration. Families should attend the information session and apply in January–February. Ask about the specific instructional model, middle school programming, extracurricular offerings, sports, after-school care, and eighth-grade high school transition planning. For West Roxbury families who want a K–8 pilot school experience, Lyndon K–8 is the primary option in the neighborhood.

schools.name: Ohrenberger Elementary
schools.address: 175 West Boundary Road, West Roxbury, MA 02132
schools.admissions: Home-based assignment. Gifted and Talented program may have additional identification process.
schools.summary: William H. Ohrenberger School stands out among West Roxbury elementary schools for offering a Gifted and Talented program — a relatively uncommon distinction within BPS's elementary portfolio. For families with children who demonstrate high academic ability or exceptional intellectual curiosity, the presence of a dedicated GT program means their child can receive instruction paced and pitched to their needs rather than being held back in a standard classroom. Families interested in the Gifted and Talented program should inquire about the identification and eligibility process, as GT programs typically have specific criteria and may require teacher recommendation or assessment. The school serves approximately 310 students in grades PK–6 in West Roxbury's residential community, drawing a student body that reflects the neighborhood's increasing diversity. Full-day K2 and limited pre-K programming are available. Home-based assignment gives West Roxbury residents priority. Ohrenberger is one of the more sought-after elementary options in West Roxbury for families who prioritize academic challenge, and families with high-ability students should put this school near the top of their list.

schools.name: Another Course to College
schools.operational_notes: IMPORTANT: BPS has announced formal closure of Another Course to College. Verify current status before applying.
schools.summary: Another Course to College (ACC) is a BPS pilot high school in Brighton that historically offered a distinctive project-based and alternative learning model. Families must be aware of a critical operational note: BPS has announced formal closure proceedings for Another Course to College. Before making any enrollment decisions based on ACC, families must verify the school's current operating status directly with BPS at bostonpublicschools.org. Do not rely on this school for long-term high school planning without confirmed current status. Families currently enrolled at ACC should actively seek transition planning support from BPS. For families seeking a confirmed pilot or alternative high school option citywide, the full range of BPS pilot high school options can be found through the BPS enrollment tool and school information sessions held in the fall semester.

schools.name: Boston Green Academy
schools.admissions: Citywide Horace Mann Charter. Apply during BPS enrollment period. Lottery when oversubscribed.
schools.operational_notes: Formerly Odyssey High School. Shares Taft building with Another Course to College.
schools.summary: Boston Green Academy Horace Mann Charter School is a BPS-funded in-district charter school serving grades 6–12 in Brighton with a distinctive focus on environmental sustainability, green careers, and ecological literacy. Formerly Odyssey High School, Boston Green Academy has built a school identity around preparing students to understand, address, and lead on the environmental challenges of the 21st century — while ensuring strong academic preparation for college and career. The sustainability focus is embedded across the curriculum: students explore environmental science, green technology, urban ecology, and climate policy alongside standard academic subjects. This interdisciplinary, mission-driven approach gives students a coherent educational narrative and purpose that can be highly motivating. As a Horace Mann Charter, the school is tuition-free and funded by BPS but operates with significant autonomy. It serves grades 6–12, allowing students to build a long-term relationship with the school from middle school through graduation. All Boston residents may apply; a lottery is held when oversubscribed. Boston Green Academy is a compelling option for students and families passionate about environmental issues who want a school where that passion is central to the educational mission, not a peripheral add-on.

schools.name: Edison K-8
schools.summary: Edison K–8 School serves kindergarten through grade 8 in Brighton with approximately 390 students, providing elementary and middle school continuity for the local community. The K–8 configuration means families can remain in one school from kindergarten through eighth grade, building stable community relationships without a separate middle school application. Brighton is a rapidly diversifying neighborhood with growing Brazilian, Chinese, and Latino communities, and Edison reflects this multilingual and multicultural character in its student body. English Learner services are an important component given the neighborhood demographics. Home-based assignment gives Brighton residents priority. Families should ask about academic programs, middle school elective offerings, sports and extracurricular activities, after-school care, and eighth-grade high school transition planning. Brighton serves a highly diverse student body reflecting Brighton's multilingual, multicultural neighborhood — the school welcomes large numbers of English Learners alongside native English speakers, and staff are experienced in supporting students from many cultural and linguistic backgrounds. Unlike standalone early education centers that serve only K0/K1, Baldwin ELPA extends through K2 (full-day kindergarten), providing a more complete early childhood journey before students transition to an elementary school. Pilot status allows Baldwin ELPA to pursue innovative early childhood pedagogies — potentially including play-based learning, inquiry-based approaches, or specialized developmental frameworks — beyond standard BPS programming. For Brighton families who want to start their child's educational journey in a school with pilot-level innovation, Baldwin ELPA is a unique opportunity. Baldwin ELPA is an excellent early childhood option for Brighton families who want an innovative, community-focused school for their youngest children.

schools.summary: Horace Mann School for the Deaf and Hard of Hearing is one of the oldest and most important specialized schools in the BPS portfolio, serving students who are deaf or hard of hearing from pre-K through grade 12. The school is a citywide placement for BPS students with significant hearing-related disabilities, providing an educational environment specifically designed for their language, communication, and academic needs. In 2025, Dr. Michelle Eisan-Smith made history as the school's first Deaf principal in its 151-year existence — a milestone of profound cultural significance signaling a new era of Deaf leadership and identity at the school. The school serves students through multiple communication modalities including American Sign Language (ASL), oral/auditory approaches, and total communication, recognizing that Deaf and hard-of-hearing students have diverse communication needs and preferences. The Horace Mann community is deeply connected to Deaf culture and identity, making it not just an educational placement but a cultural community for students and families. Placement is coordinated through BPS's Specialized Services office as part of a student's IEP process — families of children with hearing-related disabilities should contact BPS's Child Find and Specialized Services teams to initiate an evaluation and placement discussion. Horace Mann is not a school for hearing students without disabilities. For families of Deaf or hard-of-hearing children, it is one of the most specialized and supportive educational environments in the BPS system.
